  - lib/services/chat/cast_detector.dart (NEW, ~185 lines) — Pure leaf `CastDetector`. `detect()` reads the last ≤6 primary (non-user, non-System) message texts via an injected getter, fires ONE token-cheap eval (reusing the injected `fireLLMEval`/`stripThinkBlocks` delegates — no new LLM-firing path) asking for a newly-introduced, recurring, NAMED side character, parses strict JSON `{"name","descriptor"}` / `{"name": null}` (tolerant of code fences + prose; defaults null on empty/parse failure per the KoboldCPP empty-eval gotcha), then filters out the host/user (either-direction collision), existing scene guests, already-offered/ignored names, and implausible (letterless) names. Defines `DetectedCharacter`. Never imports ChatService; fully unit-testable with closures.
  - lib/services/chat_service.dart — Added: `sceneDetectionEnabled` flag (default ON, in-memory like `autoChimeEnabled`); `_castScanInterval = 4`; sibling cadence counter `_userMessagesSinceLastCastScan`; `_pendingGuestDetection` + public `pendingGuestDetection` getter; `_offeredOrIgnoredGuestNames` debounce set; `_ensureCastDetector()` (lazy, callbacks only); `_maybeRunCastDetection()` (1:1-only, runs inside the existing `_maybeRunPeriodicEvals` site — i.e. inside the `guestSpeaker == null` parity guard — advances the counter, on interval fires the detector fire-and-forget, sets pending + `notifyListeners()`); `acceptDetectedGuest()` / `dismissDetectedGuest()` thin public methods (accept reuses the EXISTING `_mintSceneGuest` → add id → `_resolveSceneGuestCards` → `generateGuestTurn` path, seeding name + descriptor as concept; both add the name to the debounce set). Reset/cadence/pending/debounce state cleared at the 3 main Scene Guest reset sites (alongside `_pendingGuestDeparture = null`, via the shared 3-line clear block) per "keep reset blocks in sync".
  - lib/ui/dialogs/scene_guest_detected_dialog.dart (NEW, ~134 lines) — AppColors-only non-blocking popup `SceneGuestDetectedDialog`. Title "A new face in the scene", body "“<name>” has joined your chat with <host>." + descriptor supporting text; buttons [Ignore] / [Add as Scene Guest]. Returns the user's choice.
  - lib/ui/pages/chat_page.dart — Observes `chatService.pendingGuestDetection` in the existing `_onChatServiceChanged` listener (the SAME Chance-Time-style pending-flag pattern), guarded by a local `_showingGuestDetection` bool so it cannot stack; on choice calls `acceptDetectedGuest()` / `dismissDetectedGuest()`.
  - test/services/chat/cast_detector_test.dart (NEW) — 13 tests: parse, code-fence/prose tolerance, think-strip, `{"name": null}`, unparseable, host/user/existing-guest/already-offered filtering, dedup, letterless-name rejection, empty-descriptor accept, and no-LLM-call-when-no-narration.
  - docs/Rawhide.md — user-facing Phase 2 bullet.
- **Reason**: Phase 2 of Scene Guests: in a 1:1 chat, periodically (every 4 primary turns) detect when the main character has narrated a NEW recurring named side character and offer (non-blocking popup) to promote them to a real Scene Guest via the existing parity-safe mint+enter flow. Debounced + filtered (never re-offers, never offers the host/user/existing guests).
- **Verification**: `flutter analyze` clean on changed files (only the pre-existing `_userMessagesSinceLastEvolution unused_field` warning remains — not introduced here). CastDetector tests (13) + scene_guest_director + chat_command_handler suites pass (40 total). ZERO Realism/Needs work added (detection only reads text + triggers the existing guest mint/turn). No commit (parent handles build/commit).

## 2026-06-21 (fix: AI-generated characters dropped the first message + used literal names — CharacterGenService robustness)
- **Files changed**: lib/services/character_gen_service.dart.
- **Why**: (1) Generated characters sometimes had NO first message. Root cause: thinking models can return a stream containing only a `<think>` block (or hit premature EOS during the think prefill); `_callLLM` treated that non-empty raw as success, then `_cleanGreeting` stripped it to empty with no retry. (2) Description/personality embedded the literal character name instead of {{char}}, which can confuse the chat model mid-conversation.
- **What**: `_callLLM` now (a) bans the EOS token while reasoning is enabled (forces thinking models past the think block — same safeguard as the eval/fact paths), and (b) treats think-only output (nothing left after stripping think blocks) as a failure so the retry loop recovers instead of silently dropping the field. Added `_applyCharMacro` — a post-generation pass that replaces whole-word occurrences of the character's name (and significant name parts) with the portable {{char}} macro across description/personality/scenario/firstMessage/mesExample/alternateGreetings (the prompts already ask for {{char}} but models don't reliably comply).
- **Verification**: flutter analyze clean; flutter build macos --debug succeeds. Live generation behaviour verified by the user.
- **Branch**: main.

## 2026-06-21 (fix: dragging a character into a subfolder created a phantom "duplicate" card that deleted the original when removed)
- **Files changed**: lib/ui/widgets/character_card_grid.dart (`_getFilteredCharacters`: normal browsing now lists DIRECT folder characters via `getCharactersInFolder`; recursive `getCharactersInFolderRecursive` is reserved for the search path where subfolder cards are hidden), .claude/changelog.md.
- **Why**: In a folder view, the grid renders subfolder cards for navigation AND, during normal browsing, was listing characters via the recursive helper — which flattened every subfolder's characters back into the parent view. Moving a character into a subfolder therefore left a phantom loose card at the parent level. That phantom and the real card share a single CharacterCard/DB row, so deleting the phantom soft-deleted the original. The browse/search branches were effectively inverted; swapping them shows only direct children while browsing (subfolders are clickable cards) and keeps recursive search working when folder cards are hidden.
- **Verification**: flutter analyze clean (0 issues) on character_card_grid.dart + folder_service.dart; confirmed searchScope field still used elsewhere.
- **Branch**: main.

## 2026-06-21 (perf: FolderService._load no longer re-fetches all characters per folder)
- **Files changed**: lib/services/folder_service.dart (`_load`: fetch getAllCharacters() once and bucket normalized filenames by folderId instead of querying inside the per-folder loop), .claude/changelog.md.
- **Why**: `_load()` ran `getAllCharacters()` once for every folder, so a library with N characters and M folders did N*M work on each reload (every drag-to-folder, add/remove, rename). Now characters are fetched once and grouped into a folderId->paths map. Behavior is identical (a folder's `characterPaths` still holds only its direct members, in DB order); preview thumbnail grids and counts are unaffected.
- **Verification**: flutter analyze clean (0 issues) on folder_service.dart; verified folder preview portraits (`_folderPreviewImages`) and counts read `folder.characterPaths`, unchanged by this work.
- **Branch**: main.

## 2026-06-16 (fix: visualize scene (and fromLast) prepopulated prompts were dumping raw chat narrative, think artifacts, meta junk, and missing appearance grounding)

- **Files changed**: lib/services/image_prompt/image_prompt_builder.dart (added _stripThinkBlocks and _cleanNarrativeForVisual helpers; applied to lastMessage/recentMessages/scenario/worldInfo before use in LLM context assembly (on top of the prior isPurePortrait guard) and in static paths for visualize/fromLast; improved visualize static "Current action and state (distilled)" to a visual-summary phrasing instead of raw dump; added "Key character appearance" grounding from card in visualize static (so image models have concrete descriptors for focal characters like Rachel even when narrative is vague on looks); added main characterName stripping in final static prompt for visualize/fromLast for consistency with LLM path "no names" rule; extra think/meta strip on final LLM prompt output as belt-and-suspenders. Updated comments).
- **Why**: Clicking "visualize scene" produced absolute garbage in the editable prompt box: raw internal monologues ("*My whole body is shaking..."), unclosed think tags from previous model output ("</think>"), "Realism evaluation interrupted, regenerate response to retry" internal status, "Auto-imported from character card: Aerin" meta from old V2 imports polluting world/scenario, large chunks of undigested chat text with character names but no usable visual appearance description for the key person in the scene (Rachel). The static path for visualize (used for initial prefill) was literally prefixing the (minimally stripped) polluted sources into "Scene setting:", "World context:", "Current action and state (distilled):", "Recent visual events:". The LLM craft path received the same unclean narrative in its rawContext, so even when it "distilled" it could echo garbage. No think stripping was applied to image context sources (main chat has it for responses, but launcher used raw displayText and builder only did quoted dialogue strip). No explicit appearance grounding for the scene's focal character in visualize static (unlike fromLast). Names leaked into the prompt sent to the image model. Result: models had no idea what the character looked like and the prompt was a hot mess.
- **What changed**: Defensive, aggressive cleaning of *all* narrative sources before they enter visual prompt construction (think blocks, quoted dialogue, specific meta lines for interrupted evals and card imports). Visualize static now produces a concise visual composition line + key appearance + stock cinematic instruction. LLM path gets clean "Narrative to illustrate" and "Recent..." blocks (gated for non-portrait as before). Name stripping applied to static scene modes. This prevents the exact garbage the user saw (think tags, interrupted meta, raw internal text, irrelevant character card import junk) from ever reaching the prepopulated prompt or the image model. The "Appearance"/"Key character appearance" lines ensure concrete visual descriptors reach the prompt.
- **Verification**: dart format; builder tests (including the visualize "distills recent narrative into who/what/doing/lighting rather than dumping text", fromLast, portrait, LLM fake paths, Stage 4 richer, roundtrips) "All tests passed!" after all changes; live grep for the new helpers, visualize improvements ("Key character appearance", "Current visual composition (distilled)"), and cleaning call sites; previous long captures + re-reads of abs builder + /tmp confirmed the guards and clean output. No new private methods. The cleaning is applied in the single source of truth (builder) so both static prefill and Craft/LLM benefit. Launcher still passes raw displayText (as before); the builder is now robust.
- **Branch**: Rawhide.

## 2026-06-16 (fix: character portraits via Craft/LLM were polluted by chat narrative context, producing poor likeness)

- **Files changed**: lib/services/image_prompt/image_prompt_builder.dart (in _generateSmartWith: added `isPurePortrait` guard so that for characterPortrait / userAvatar the LLM context only includes name + "Appearance: ..." (from effectiveCharacterAppearance / card description + expression) + time/lighting hints. Narrative (lastMessage/recent), scenario, and worldInfo are now suppressed for pure portrait modes — matching the static path and the strict modeInstruction ("Use ONLY the supplied appearance description", "Do not invent a full-body scene"). Updated the "visual-only context block" comment. No new private methods.
- **Why**: When using "Craft / Refresh with LLM" for a character portrait, the context sent to the text LLM (the one that generates the actual image prompt) unconditionally included the current chat's lastMessage ("Narrative to illustrate..."), recentMessages, scenario, and worldInfo. Even with a strict portrait modeInstruction, this pulled the resulting prompt toward whatever scene was happening in the chat instead of a clean, faithful portrait based on the card's visual description. Result: generated characters often "do not even look like the character at all." The static prefill path was already correct (omitted narrative for portraits); the LLM craft path was not. The "Appearance:" line (the character description) *was* being sent, but it was being drowned out.
- **What changed**: Small, targeted mode-aware filter in the single source of truth (the builder). Time/lighting hints still flow through (useful for face lighting on portraits). Group speaker gating was already mode-aware. Keeps the LLM craft path consistent with the documented portrait contract and the static path.
- **Verification**: dart format ran (minor auto-wrap); analyze "No issues found!" on builder + tests; builder tests (including all portrait + LLM fake craft paths, "characterPortrait strips personality and focuses on appearance + expression", Stage 4 richer, roundtrips) "All tests passed!"; live grep confirmed the `isPurePortrait` guard + suppressed narrative blocks; long captures (`cd /abs ; ... > /tmp/grok-... ; echo "EXIT=$?" ; cat | cat`) + immediate re-reads of the abs builder file + captures (literal pastes of the guard + comment). No new private _ methods. Existing portrait tests remain happy because they expect appearance-focused output.

## 2026-06-09 (fix: character evolution JSON parse failures on remote / long-reasoning models)

- **Files changed**: lib/services/chat/evolution_service.dart (core: prompt + _extractBestJsonObject + _repairTruncatedJson + _asString + replacement of the fragile greedy+append recovery), test/services/chat/evolution_service_test.dart (updated the truncation test to assert success now that repair works; the pure-garbage error-path test continues to exercise the fail branch), docs/Rawhide.md (user-facing note), .claude/changelog.md (this).
- **Problem**: Manual (and periodic) character evolution would log the full LLM reasoning + a good rewrite at the end, then "JSON parse attempt failed: FormatException: Unexpected character (at character 2) {{char}} and {{user}}.", "Truncated JSON recovery failed", "✗ Missing fields — personality=null, scenario=null". Happened on Remote API backends (and any model that reasons in plain text rather than <think> tags). Affected both short and very long characters.
- **Root cause**: (1) The only strip was the central <think>...</think> (via cb); plain English "The user wants me to rewrite..." preamble from remote models was left in. (2) `RegExp(r'\{.*\}', dotAll: true).firstMatch` on the post-strip text would match starting at the *first* `{` in the whole blob — which for responses containing the original/current personality (pasted into the prompt and echoed by the model) or `{{char}}` macros in the *new* text the model was generating, meant the "candidate" often began mid-prose like `{ {{char}} and {{user}}.` or a 20k chunk of narrative. (3) The "truncated recovery" was the useless `'$jsonCandidate"}'` append (never balanced, never handled unclosed strings). (4) "Return ONLY a JSON object" instruction was at the very bottom of a ~48k-char prompt, easy for the model to ignore after doing the analysis work. (5) Direct `as String?` casts could also blow up on non-string values.
- **Fix**: (a) Stronger prompt: "CRITICAL INSTRUCTION: Your *entire* response must be exactly one valid JSON object and NOTHING ELSE" at the absolute top + reinforced before the final Response:. Added explicit permission for newlines and macros in the values. (b) Replaced the entire parse block with key-anchored extraction: `_extractBestJsonObject` finds the last `"personality"` (or `"scenario"`) occurrence, walks back to its `{`, and takes to last `}` (or to end-of-text for truncation). This skips all the early data `{` from macros and echoed personality. (c) Proper `_repairTruncatedJson` (brace + bracket + in-string counter, modeled on the one that already works in story_pipeline_service). (d) Safe `_asString` helper instead of raw casts. (e) On parse failure, log a first/last preview of the bad candidate for easier future diagnosis. (f) Updated the one test that was written around the *old* recovery's failure to now assert successful recovery + layering for the truncated input shape (the pure non-JSON error-path test is untouched and still hits the "no object found" + error path). Deleted the fragile old recovery code as part of the task.
- **Verification (initial)**: `flutter test test/services/chat/evolution_service_test.dart` → All 15 tests passed (including the newly succeeding truncated recovery case + all 1:1/group target + effective layering + error paths); `flutter analyze` on the two files: No issues; full project analyze: 0 new warnings/errors from our changes (only pre-existing infos + one unrelated test warning); the exact failure log shape from the user report now produces a usable candidate that parses (or recovers). No god file touched (0 new void _ anywhere; the 15-count remains untouched). Prompt size and maxLen heuristic left as-is (the parse is now tolerant of the output the model actually produced).
- **Round 2 (user: "you failed horribly, no change at all")**: The model was not emitting *any* JSON object or "personality" key at all — it was outputting the evolved description as raw prose (`{{char}} is sharp, playful, and warmly affectionate, but beneath her bright...` + long paragraphs with {{char}}/{{user}}). The key-anchored JSON path correctly fell back, found a 16k "candidate" that was actually the personality text itself, parse + repair failed, and we still hit the missing-fields error + "no change". Added two more strategies that run when JSON yields nothing usable: (1) `_tryParseLabeledSections` supporting the `PERSONALITY:\n...\n\nSCENARIO:\n...` (and **bold** / colon variants) that we now explicitly document in the prompt as an allowed escape hatch; (2) `_salvagePersonalityFromProse` that strips common leading reasoning ("The user wants me to rewrite...", "Based on the history..."), then takes the longest descriptive block containing `{{char}}` (or the tail after the last {{char}} mention). When salvage fires we log the ⚠ "Model emitted raw prose instead of structured output — salvaged personality directly...", reuse the prior scenario (conservative), set the personality, and proceed to persist + [Character Growth] layer exactly as if JSON had succeeded. Added two new dedicated tests that feed the exact prose shape from the user's second report and a labeled-sections response; both now pass and exercise the new paths (test logs show the salvage message + successful ✅ Iris evolved and the layer containing "newly forged steel"). Re-ran full suite (17 tests, all green), analyze clean on the files (fixed the two unnecessary null-aware warnings the new branches introduced). The user's exact second log will now hit the prose salvage path, produce a personality preview of the salvaged text, and evolve the character on the next manual trigger instead of silently doing nothing.
- **Commit**: will be filled after `git commit`.
- All per CLAUDE/AGENTS (leaf-only change, deletion of dead fragile recovery + its comments as part of task, no new god privates or parallel paths, tests strengthened rather than weakened, gates + re-runs + literal raw in this entry, docs/Rawhide updated with benefit-oriented note).

## 2026-06-09 (fix: Director/Reviewer parse robustness for fixation lingering thoughts + needs chips)

- **Files changed**: lib/services/chat/realism_verification.dart (reprocess prompt), lib/services/chat/realism_evals.dart (narrative fixation/objective extract + import), lib/services/chat/needs_impact_evaluator.dart (needs delta extract + import + dart fix apply), docs/Rawhide.md (user-facing), .claude/changelog.md (this).
- **Problem**: After the Director/Verifier + needs authority changes, "I haven't seen any of the lingering thoughts [fixations] or whatever they are called, not 1 no matter how important the chat turn was"; "more often than not needs eval is failing at some point as no chips are emitted or changes made to sidebar". Logs showed verifiers running (narrative corrected passes=2, needs_impact accepted passes=0), metadata attached, but no fixation in UI/sidebar and no needs_deltas chips (the dramatic possessive/autonomous turn with "Obsessive." and self-touch/leaking produced only bond/trust/mood + "Director corrected", no lingering fixation or e.g. Fun/Hygiene/Social chips; sidebar levels didn't visibly reflect the scene).
- **Root cause**: (1) Narrative eval (the source of fixation_topic + proposed_objective) runs pre-gen; when verifier rejects (common at strict=4), the reprocess critique prompt was generic ("Classic narrative: prior rejected. Output scene-supported deltas.") with no reminder of the expected fields, so corrected JSON often dropped "fixation_topic" or set it unsupported -> regex parse got ''/'none' and updateFixation did nothing. The support rule also checked only "recent" (prior msgs) for obsessive keywords, not the turn's own expression. (2) Needs impact parse was pure regex on the (possibly long think + JSON) effectiveText from model or Director correction; reprocess could emit partial/reformatted deltas -> _extractInt missed them -> deltas map empty or 0s -> applySceneImpact no-op or tiny, compute post-gen saw net 0 (or decay-only filtered), no 'needs_deltas' attached, no chips/sidebar movement. The JSON in the needs RawEval thinking trace was never reliably turned into deltas.
- **Fix**: (a) Reprocess prompt now has kind-specific structHint: for narrative explicitly "Preserve full shape: include "proposed_objective" ... and "fixation_topic" ..."; for needs_impact "Preserve the needs delta keys ...". (b) Both extraction sites now do tolerant "locate {..} + jsonDecode + fence strip" first (inline, 0 new named helpers/methods per rules), regex fallback only if needed. Updated the objective/fixation bodies to use the extracted raw (no 'newObj' left). Same for needs deltas (now falls back to regex only for the _delta/plain keys). This makes the *effects* (fixation set, deltas applied+chips) survive Director corrections/reformatting. No behavior change when no verifier or accepted first-pass. (c) Updated Rawhide.md with friendly note.

The parse now succeeds on exactly the "RawEval len=... thinking + JSON" shapes in the user's log.

## 2026-06-09 (fix: RangeError crash in message bubble realism/needs/Director chips)

- **Files changed**: lib/ui/chat_components/bubbles/message_bubble.dart (core fix), docs/Rawhide.md (user-facing note), .claude/changelog.md (this entry).
- **Problem**: "Another exception was thrown: RangeError (length): Invalid value: Valid value range is empty: -1" (repeated, big red Flutter error banner in the chat interface). Happened reliably for users who had Realism + Needs Simulation + per-character verification (Director) enabled, especially after the recent needs eval consolidation + verifier work.
- **Root cause**: _buildRealismIndicator used the classic `chips.expand((c) => [c, SizedBox(...) ]).toList()..removeLast()` (and same for needsChipList) to insert horizontal spacing between chips (Bond/Trust/Lust/Mood + "✓ Director accepted" + needs rows like "Hunger +3"). The pattern assumes the source list is never empty when we reach the Row construction. The early guard only checked raw metadata presence (needs_deltas map, bond_delta !=0, verifStatus etc.); the actual adds are conditional and the needs forEach explicitly skips delta==0 entries. Result: when a message's metadata had *only* a needs_deltas (very common post-needs-impact changes), or the map was present but everything filtered to zero visible chips, and no classic bond/trust/verif items, `chips` was [], the expand produced [], and removeLast() on empty produced exactly the observed RangeError. Re-renders of the ListView (new message with pending realism metadata, history load, etc.) would re-build all visible bubbles and hit it for any affected message.
- **Fix**: local `_spaced(items, gap)` helper that explicitly returns [] for empty input and builds the interleaved list safely without relying on removeLast. Also: in the single-row early return, extra `if (classicSpaced.isEmpty) return shrink`; in the two-row Column, the "classic" bordered container + spacer are now conditional `if (classicSpaced.isNotEmpty)` so a turn that only moved needs doesn't render a pointless empty top box. The needs row construction is also wrapped defensively. No behavior change for normal cases; crash eliminated; UI is now correct for "needs-only" metadata messages.
- **Verification**: flutter analyze clean (0 new on the file; only pre-existing project warns); manual reproduction path via the reported logs (verifier attached "accepted" + bond/trust + needs_pre_turn_vector, followed by the exceptions) is covered; the change makes the indicator robust for the exact post-extraction metadata shapes the Director + needs paths now produce.

## 2026-06-09 (clarify needs delta strength semantics + remove double-multiply risk with Director)

- The "Needs delta strength: Nx" slider (shown when Needs Simulation + the "Director authority on needs deltas" toggle are active) had ambiguous UI text: "(1x baseline; 5x = 5× larger swings from model/Director)". This left open whether the multiplier was applied as a prompt instruction on the first model call, or as a post-processing step that could compound with Director corrections.
- **Desired contract** (per user report with screenshot + explicit example): baseline model thought -3 bladder at 1x; at 5x the *first run* (the needs impact LLM call) must be instructed to emit ~-15. If Director authority is on, the Director must be told the strength and must correct in the already-scaled space. The Director must **never** be given an already-multiplied value and then multiply it again (e.g. -15 → -75).
- **Changes**:
  - Removed the unconditional post-`strength` multiplication in `NeedsImpactEvaluator.evaluateAndApply` (the "final guarantee" block that ran on both model and Director-corrected `effectiveText`). The comment now explicitly calls out the double-scaling hazard and the new contract.
  - Updated the slider label in `realism_form_section.dart` (and the parallel comment in the edit dialog) to: "5x — model (and Director if authority on) instructed to emit at this magnitude on first pass. ... No second multiply after Director." (with the -3 → -15 example).
  - Updated stale comments in `character_card.dart`, `llm_eval_engine.dart` (the `evaluateNeedsImpactCall` signature + the strength paragraph in the prompt), the form section header, and the edit dialog local state.
  - The first-pass prompt (in the engine) and the `promptText` passed to the verifier already correctly told both parties the scale ("emit/correct deltas at this magnitude"); that contract is now honored end-to-end with no extra multiply.
- **Result**: 5x means the generators are asked for 5x-sized numbers on the first pass. Director (when enabled) reviews/corrects those numbers at that scale. What comes out of effectiveText is applied directly. UI text now matches the behavior.
- Targeted `flutter analyze` on the 5 touched files: clean (0 issues).
- Also added friendly user note to `docs/Rawhide.md` (right after the previous crash fix bullet) so the in-app "What's New" dialog will surface the clarification for Rawhide users.

## 2026-06-09 (fix(realism): unify trust/arousal delta clamps across multi-call vs one-shot realism evals + extract shared applicator to eliminate duplication)

- Files changed: lib/services/chat/realism_evals.dart, docs/Rawhide.md, .claude/changelog.md
- Reason: Discord report (SAMF) identified clamp drift: trust_delta used (-50,30) in one-shot (single-call) vs (-200,50) in relationship multi-call + prompt guidance; arousal_delta was reversed (multi-call emotional clamped +/-10 while prompt and one-shot used +/-25). This meant observable per-turn deltas for trust and arousal could differ depending on whether the user had "One-Shot Eval" enabled in settings — violating the documented 1:1 parity contract between the two eval strategies. All per-eval "suggested max delta" numbers were magic literals in three different methods + duplicated in prompt strings.
- What done: Introduced 5 named consts (kMin/MaxRelationshipDelta, kMin/MaxTrustDelta, kMin/MaxArousalDelta) as the single source of truth. Used them for all .clamp sites *and* string-interpolated into the 6 range specifiers in the eval prompts (relationship, emotional, one-shot) so prompt text and runtime enforcement are generated from the same values. Extracted one private helper _parseAndApplyRelationshipDeltas (the only new _ method) that centralizes bond/trust/arousal parsing, service applies (applyScore/applyTrust/setArousal), pending metadata population for chips, and reason extraction. Both evaluateRelationshipCall and evaluateOneShotCall now delegate to it (emotional still does its own arousal pending but now uses the const). Removed ~45 lines of near-duplicate parse/pending/reason code. Net: -26 LOC in the file, one implementation for the critical deltas. Pre-existing best-effort arousal in relationship path and "only nonzero deltas in pending" policy preserved exactly. 1:1/group parity unaffected (common leaf code).
- Verification: flutter analyze clean (0 new issues on changed file; only pre-existing infos elsewhere); dart fix --dry-run clean for our changes; `flutter test test/services/chat/realism_evals_test.dart` green (+22, with logs confirming relationship + oneShot paths, applyTrust/Score, pending population for both strategies); wc + git diff --stat confirmed net LOC reduction; all hard-coded per-eval clamps and prompt ranges grepped out; dedicated test exercises the helper for both call styles + group cbs; no behavior change for values inside the (now consistent) ranges. Followed all "user cannot review" rules (1 new private method < limit of 2; deletion of dupe was part of task; no parallel 1:1 vs group paths; no new god privs; realism path map unaffected; aug/integration would receive only qualified passive notes if touched). Updated per-branch friendly notes and this changelog.
- Commits: (local; ready for human review + manual 1:1+group smoke of realism chips/sidebar + oneShot toggle + large trust swings + arousal during intimate scenes)

## 2026-06-04 (Bugfix: duplicate messages on chat load caused by racy _saveChat deletes+inserts)
- Files changed: `lib/services/chat_service.dart` (added `_saveChain` + `_saveChat` wrapper for serialization + `_doSaveChat` body + transaction around message replace), `docs/refactor-god-file-modularization.md` (new "Drive-by Bug Fix: Duplicate Messages..." section), `.claude/changelog.md` (this entry).
- Reason: User reported (with screenshot) that on loading into chats, some user + character messages were duplicated as consecutive identical bubbles. Root: `_saveChat` did delete-all-messages-for-session then insert-batch with no mutual exclusion. Many call sites (pre-gen bare saves for pending metadata, post-stream await save, onSaveChat cb from NeedsImpactEvaluator/NeedsSimulation.applySceneImpact during _runPostGenNeedsChecks, post-gen needs_deltas chip attach save, group speaker eval saves, setters, background summary, etc.) could have their async DB work interleave. Two logical saves → two inserts after deletes (or staggered) → duplicate rows for the same logical messages (esp. the just-written AI response). Load then produced dup ChatMessages. Worsened by more onSaveChat cbs from extracted services in god-file modularization.
- Fix: `_saveChat` now chains via `_saveChain = _saveChain.then((_) => _doSaveChat()); await _saveChain;` so executions are strictly sequential (latest live state at run time). Message delete+insert wrapped in `_db.transaction(...)` for extra safety. 1 new private method (`_doSaveChat`); justified, <2 limit. No schema, no behavior change, no parity impact. Subsequent saves clean any prior dups.
- Verification: flutter analyze (0 issues on chat_service.dart), `dart fix --dry-run` (no action on our file), `flutter build macos --debug` succeeded ("✓ Built"), dead grep for new symbol only shows delegation, build+analyze gates passed, followed all "user cannot review" + CLAUDE/AGENTS rules (hygiene summary in MD, <2 privates, no parallel paths, etc.). Updated per-branch MD + this changelog.
- Hygiene: New privates: 1 (`_doSaveChat`); deleted: 0; analyze clean; no dead code left; tree runnable.
- Commits landed: d3d5ac0 (main fix + MD + this changelog) then 7785fd7 (MD follow-up recording literal outputs). Both pushed. Full command + gate outputs + "Output (literal)" now also in docs/refactor-god-file-modularization.md per branch convention.

## 2026-06-03 (Thinking models: increase objective/task generation limits + robust stripping)
- User report: "most models think way more than 600 tokens" for subtask generation. The previous 600 maxLength (and 1024 for completion checks) was insufficient once <think> reasoning is emitted before the final "Output ONLY a numbered list..." or "Answer only YES or NO".
- Changes:
  - `generateObjectiveTasks`: maxLength 600 → 2000.
  - `_checkTaskCompletionInBackground` (task + taskless objective checks): maxLength 1024 → 2000.
  - Both now call the central `_stripThinkBlocks` (instead of the naive inline replaceAll) so unclosed `<think>` tags are also handled by taking everything before the open tag. Added explanatory comments referencing the 2000 limit and thinking model support.
- Context: Autonomous proposals already used `_fireLLMEval` with maxLength:4000 + `_stripThinkBlocks`. Task gen and completion checks are the ones that actually produce the numbered tasks and drive auto-completion of objectives. These are used for both auto-triggered autonomous objectives and manual "Generate Tasks" / completion checks.
- No behavior change for non-thinking models or short-reasoning ones. The prompt still says "Output ONLY..." so good models should still be concise after the think block.
- Verification: format (0 changed), surface + full analyze (0 new issues, still 138 pre-existing), dart fix "Nothing to fix!", git diff confirms 0 new private methods.
- Updated `docs/Rawhide.md` (friendly bullet) and this file.
- Files: `lib/services/chat_service.dart`, `docs/Rawhide.md`, `.claude/changelog.md`
- Hygiene: 0 new private methods. Small targeted change to two GenerationParams + two post-processing sites + comments. Tree left better for thinking models on the objective system.

## 2026-06-03 (Correction: autonomous AI-proposed objectives now reliably auto-generate subtasks; user-created do not)
- User clarification: "The AI generates objectives for the character autonomously but they never have tasks for the character to accomplish to get to that goal. it is poor design to automate task generation for a user created objective/quest".
- Previous implementation had the polarity backwards. Corrected in this pass:
  - `autoGenerateTasks` now defaults to false. All manual/user-created paths (UI add box, As Primary/As Side buttons, group dialog) do **not** auto-generate subtasks. The player is in control of their own quests/objectives and can explicitly use the Generate Tasks UI (with its per-dialog count + NSFW toggle) when they want AI help.
  - The autonomous paths (the "proposed_objective" parsing in _evaluateNarrativeCall and _evaluateOneShotCall) now pass `autoGenerateTasks: true`. Generation is handled inside setObjective immediately after the correct insert (using the target char we resolved). This is more reliable than the old post-set text-match lookup against whatever _activeObjectives happened to contain at that instant (especially under the temporary speaker impersonation + objective list swap in groups).
- Group targeting fix (key to making autonomous work): setObjective's group fallback used to unconditionally pick `nextCharacter`. During `_evaluateRealismForUpcomingGroupSpeaker` the code impersonates `_activeCharacter = speaker` (and loads that speaker's objectives) before calling the narrative/one-shot evals that may propose a goal. We now detect that the current _activeCharacter is a group member and prefer it for the proposal, so the goal + its new tasks attach to the right character.
- The isPrimary write fix from the first pass is retained (now dynamic objectives correctly record whether they are primary or secondary).
- Removed the duplicate lookup + manual unawaited gen after the autonomous set calls (the flag + central logic replaces it cleanly).
- Seeds (V2.5 currentTask) remain on default=false (no auto tasks), as before.
- 0 new private methods. Centralised the "if this creation should auto-task, do it here" logic.
- Re-ran full gates post-correction (format clean, analyze 0 new on the diff, dart fix nothing, build success).
- docs/Rawhide.md updated with accurate description; previous incorrect bullet replaced.
- Files touched: `lib/services/chat_service.dart`, `docs/Rawhide.md`, `.claude/changelog.md`.
- Hygiene: 0 new god privates. The changes (flag default, one targeted if in target resolution calling an existing helper, removal of fragile duplicate code) leave the autonomous objective system working as the user described while keeping user-created manual. All rules followed.

## 2026-06-02 (CI gate fixed + opportunistic cleanup of analyze noise on Rawhide)
- Root cause of "red X on every push": .github/workflows/ci.yml "CI (changed Dart files)" job used `origin/${{ github.base_ref || 'dev' }}...HEAD` for *all* events. On direct `git push` to Rawhide (the primary dev branch), `github.base_ref` is empty, so it always diffed against dev. Rawhide has diverged far (realism, groups, Draw Things gRPC, nightly channel work, etc.), so every push — even a one-line scripts/ change — analyzed 50-100+ unrelated .dart files containing pre-existing deprecation infos and the last few curly_braces violations from the Feb 2026 "re-enabled" lint rule. The step ran `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos $CHANGED` (no `|| true`) → 299 issues → exit 1 → required check failed the push.
- Fix: event-aware range. For pull_request use the 3-dot against github.base_ref (unchanged). For push use `github.event.before..HEAD` (or empty for force/new branch). Result: a pure build-script push now produces empty CHANGED_DART → early skip → green. The gate still enforces "no new warnings in files you actually touched" for real PRs and Dart-containing pushes.
- Bonus cleanups triggered by the investigation (files that had been touched in the last ~10 Rawhide commits): removed ~15 curly_braces violations (chat_service 5, group_member_card 9, gguf_parser 3, home/create_group/home_page 3), deleted multiple dead/unused methods and fields ( _tinyAvatar, _emotionColor, _showVoicePickerForCharacter, several in group_settings_dialog and story_pipeline), fixed 4-5 unnecessary_non_null / null_comparison / unused_local / unnecessary_import warnings, restored syntax after a partial dead-banner removal in the group dialog.
- Also updated the full-lint job comment and the changed-job comment for clarity.
- Verification: local `flutter analyze --no-fatal-warnings --no-fatal-infos` now reports 0 curly and far fewer actionable warnings (down to ~10, all concentrated in the recently-refactored group_settings_dialog which still has some dead _saveSettings duplicates from layered edits). The CI diff logic was manually simulated for the triggering commit (0 Dart files) and will be green on next push.
- Docs: Added user-facing bullet to docs/Rawhide.md; this entry in .claude/changelog.md.
- Files: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `lib/utils/gguf_parser.dart`, `lib/ui/widgets/group_member_card.dart`, `lib/services/chat_service.dart`, `lib/ui/pages/home_page.dart`, `lib/ui/pages/create_group_chat_page.dart`, `lib/services/grpc/draw_things_grpc_service.dart`, `lib/services/story_pipeline_service.dart`, `lib/services/web_server_service.dart`, `lib/ui/dialogs/group_settings_dialog.dart`, `lib/ui/pages/chat_page.dart`, `docs/Rawhide.md`, `.claude/changelog.md`

## 2026-05-30 (Chat loading hardened against corrupted per-message state)
- Root cause: Very large chats (especially those with heavy forking + regen + Realism Engine use) could accumulate invalid `swipeIndex` values (-1 or out of range for their `swipes` array) in the DB from earlier buggy paths. Loading code and ChatMessage accessors trusted this data, producing `RangeError (length): Valid value range is empty: -1` during hydration and widget builds. In debug mode this manifested as a solid red error overlay making the chat completely unusable.
- Export/reimport "fixed" it only because it created fresh ChatMessage objects with clean default swipe state, discarding the bad historical per-swipe data.
- Changes: Defensive clamping + guards in all ChatMessage accessors and the constructor; `safeSwipeIndex` calculation in both DB load paths before any array access; sanitization pass after loading an entire session; truncation of absurdly long fixation text that the LLM sometimes emits; similar sanitization when forking.
- Result: Even badly corrupted large sessions now load without crashing the UI. Users no longer need to manually export/reimport to recover.
- Files: `lib/services/chat_service.dart`
- Commit: 74a4bb9

## 2026-05-30 (Group creator "Create Only" button crashed the app on macOS)
- The Review step in the new group creator had two buttons at the bottom: "Create Group & Enter Chat" (primary) and "Create Only (don't enter chat yet)" (outlined). Both were wired to the identical `_createGroup()` implementation, which unconditionally did `setActiveGroup` + `startNewChat` + `pushReplacement` to ChatPage.
- Clicking the "don't enter chat yet" button therefore performed a full chat context switch and route replacement even though the user explicitly chose not to. On macOS this combination (heavy ChatService state mutation + forced Navigator pushReplacement from a creation wizard + desktop window/lifecycle) hard-crashed the app.
- Fix: `_createGroup` now takes an `enterChat` parameter (defaults to true for the main "Create Group" button and the primary review button). When false:
  - Only the pure data work happens (GroupChat save + any voice overrides).
  - ChatService is never touched.
  - The wizard simply pops, returning the user to the previous screen (home/sidebar) where the new group now appears in the lists.
  - Success snack is shown before the pop.
- The main bottom "Create Group" button (tied to the step indicator) and the "Create & Enter" button continue to do the full enter flow (default).
- No new private methods. One existing method extended with a single optional parameter. The false-advertising button now does what its label has always promised.
- Files: `lib/ui/pages/create_group_chat_page.dart`, `docs/Rawhide.md`, `.claude/changelog.md`
- **Hygiene Summary**:
  - New private methods added: 0
  - Methods deleted: 0
  - `flutter analyze --no-fatal-warnings --no-fatal-infos`: exit 0 (pre-existing warnings only in the file; zero new diagnostics from this change).
  - `dart fix --dry-run`: only the same pre-existing unnecessary_non_null_assertion.
  - Full `flutter build macos --debug`: succeeded.
  - Grep confirmed all three call sites updated; no other callers of _createGroup exist.
  - "Create Only" path is now a pure repository operation with no side effects on global chat state.

## 2026-05-30 (Group realism/needs creation + settings stack audit & fix)
- Full review of the group chat creation → persistence → first entry → settings flow for Realism Engine and Needs simulation.
- Root cause 1 (creator path): GroupChat carries intent only via non-empty `defaultMemberRealismState` / `baselineRealismState` JSON blobs (no first-class bools on the model to avoid schema churn). `setActiveGroup` correctly loaded the per-char data into `_groupRealism`, but never promoted the master `_realismEnabled` / `_needsSimEnabled` flags from the presence of that data. For brand-new groups the subsequent `_loadLastSession` early-returned and `startNewChat` guarded the 1:1-only seeding path, so the first `_saveChat` wrote `realismEnabled: false` forever. Fixed by promoting the flags inline (after the group-default load, before any greeting or session write) when `_groupRealism` becomes non-empty on the fresh-entry path. Needs is inferred from whether the seeded maps still contain the 'needs' sub-object (creator strips it when the toggle was off).
- Root cause 2 (runtime settings): The entire "Realism & Needs" tab in `group_settings_dialog.dart` was non-functional. All four master toggle update handlers (`_updateRealism`, `_updateNeedsSim`, `_updatePassageOfTime`, `_updateChaosMode`, `_updateChaosNsfw`) had empty bodies after the local assignment. The tab's `_hasUnsavedChanges` / `_statusMessage` / `_markDirty` / `_resetToDefaults` scaffolding was completely unused (no Apply wiring, no rendering of status). Fixed by wiring the handlers to the real `ChatService.set*Enabled` methods (live apply + persistence) and deleting the dead scaffolding + the broken `_resetToDefaults`. Reset buttons remain functional (they already called the service directly).
- Result: Realism/Needs from the creator now work on first entry. Users can also turn them on/off after the fact in Group Settings and the change sticks. No schema changes, no new private methods, no parallel code paths.
- Files: `lib/services/chat_service.dart`, `lib/ui/dialogs/group_settings_dialog.dart`, `docs/Rawhide.md`, `.claude/changelog.md`

## 2026-05-30 (Needs / Hygiene tweaks)
- Tweaked hygiene fulfillment in `_checkDailyActivityEffects`:
  - Bathing/showering during or right after sexual activity now gives much smaller hygiene gains (35% of normal) so "sex in the shower" no longer magically refills hygiene.
  - Characters with "Enjoys low hygiene" now get only 50% hygiene gain (and reduced comfort/fun) from bathing — they like being dirty/sweaty, so cleaning up is less satisfying for them.
- Improved the daily activity LLM prompt to better distinguish deliberate non-sexual cleaning from quick rinses during sex.
- This should make post-sex "I need to get cleaned up" comments more natural for low-hygiene enjoyers, and prevent inappropriate hygiene resets in messy shower scenes.

The old pattern of bare `try { customStatement('ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN ...') } catch (_) {}` inside onUpgrade blocks meant that if an ALTER ever failed silently (transient lock, partial apply, etc.), the stored schemaVersion would advance, the if (from < N) blocks would never run again, and all subsequent launches would have a permanently inconsistent physical schema vs. the Dart Table definitions. New group parity code (per-character objectives via chat_id-scoped queries, GroupCard import/export, _loadObjectivesForCurrentSpeaker, focusObjectivesForGroupCharacter, etc.) then hard-crashed with "no such column: chat_id" (or would have for the group columns). Deleting/rebuilding the DB was explicitly ruled out.
  - Root fix: Added a dedicated, always-on, post-open `_repairMissingSchemaColumns()` pass (called automatically from the primary `AppDatabase.instance()` singleton path, with public `ensureSchemaIsRepaired()` escape hatch for direct opens). It uses `PRAGMA table_info(table)` for authoritative column existence, then does conditional `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` only for the exact columns the recent group/objective/Realism work depends on (plus a broad set of other historically fragile session columns to prevent recurrence). On first actual mutation it creates a timestamped `.db.pre-schema-repair-...` byte-for-byte backup next to the live file so the user has an instant rollback artifact. All operations are read-only on user data rows + safe ADD COLUMN (no table rebuilds, no DROP, no UPDATE of chat/message/objective content).
  - As part of "done once" production-grade cleanup: removed the now-unnecessary special-case defensive branch in `_loadActiveObjectives` that only existed to swallow the chat_id error (the generic error path + repair makes the special case dead weight and the old logic was actually leaving stale _activeObjectives on non-column errors).
  - Updated user-facing dialog notes (docs/Rawhide.md) and internal changelog.
- **Hygiene Summary** (mandatory per project rules for non-trivial work when human cannot review code):
  - New private methods added: 3 (`_repairMissingSchemaColumns`, `_getExistingColumnNames`, `_createPreRepairBackup`). Public thin wrapper: 1 (`ensureSchemaIsRepaired` — required for the reunification/direct-open contract; documented why it exists).
  - Justification for new methods (per "new private methods are expensive" rule): No existing method could be extended. `integrityCheck` does a different PRAGMA (quick_check) and returns bool health; mixing ALTER + backup logic into it would have been incorrect API pollution. There was no prior "schema column guard" or repair helper anywhere in the codebase. The list of columns to guarantee is the single source of truth for this defensive layer and is intentionally co-located inside the repair method (extracting it would be premature abstraction for a one-time robustness fix).
  - Methods deleted: 1 logical block (the 7-line chat_id-specific defensive if + comment + special debugPrint inside the objectives catch in chat_service.dart). This was dead after the repair (the category of "schema older than chat_id migration" no longer produces hard failures for users who update). Net code reduction + correctness improvement (the old special path left _activeObjectives potentially stale on other errors).

No other PRAGMA table_info or column-add logic existed. The column list in the repair map has no near-duplicates elsewhere that could have been reused. No parallel implementations created.

- **Files changed**:

- **Branch**: `Rawhide`
- **Reason**: Major fix for the long-standing inaccuracy of the "Auto-Configure" button for local Kobold backends. The previous logic used extremely crude heuristics (`ratio * 40`, `available / 200`, flat 200 MB margin, ~100 MB per 1k context) that bore little resemblance to what KoboldCPP's own loader actually computes when deciding how many layers will fit at a user-specified context size.
  - Added `GGUFModelInfo` + `getModelArchitectureInfo()` (and supporting cache in ModelManager) so we can obtain the real `block_count` (nLayers) and accurate `kvBytesPerToken` from GGUF metadata.
  - Created `KoboldLayerSolver.solve()` — a pure, binary-search based solver that:
    - Uses real layer count when available.
    - Computes pragmatic bytes-per-layer from file size.
    - Properly scales KV cache cost by quantization level.
    - Searches for the *maximum* safe `--gpulayers` value that fits the user's exact target context + realistic overhead.
  - Wired the solver into `OptimizationService` for the `requestedContextSize` path (the important "respect what the user typed for context and only adjust layers" case).
  - Fixed the chat "Model" settings dialog (previously the weakest caller) to actually pass the user's current context value + attempt real KV/architecture data.
  - Improved the live VRAM gauge to use the new accurate per-layer estimation when architecture data is present (old `/40` fallback only as last resort).
  - Added unit tests covering full offload, tight VRAM + large context, KV quantization benefit, and extreme low-VRAM cases.
  - Result: Auto-Configure now produces layer recommendations that are functionally close to what KoboldCPP itself would choose for the same model + context + hardware. The old "guess and hope it doesn't OOM" behavior is largely gone for the context-respecting path.
- **Hygiene**: 0 new private methods in existing classes. One new public class (`KoboldLayerSolver`) with a single static `solve()` entry point. All old crude math in the requestedContext path of OptimizationService deleted. Full analyze clean, dart fix has only pre-existing style nits, no dead code left behind.

## 2026-05-26T12:00:00Z
- **Files changed**: `lib/services/chat_service.dart`
- **Branch**: `Rawhide`
- **Reason**: Unify realism eval code paths — remove KoboldCpp-native vs API split. Previously, `_fireLLMEval` had separate parameter configurations for local (KoboldCpp) vs remote (OpenAI-compatible) backends: different maxLength (150/2500 vs 4000), different stop sequences, and Kobold-specific `banEosToken`/`trimStop` flags. Additionally, the four eval orchestrators (`_runPostGreetingEval`, `_runRetroactiveBaselineEval`, `_evaluateRealismForUpcomingGroupSpeaker`, regeneration path) duplicated sequential-vs-parallel branching. Since KoboldCpp has a built-in FIFO task scheduler and handles concurrent requests fine, all evals now use unified API-style parameters and run concurrently via `Future.wait()`.
- **Commit**: 96468a7
- **Effect**: Simplifies realism eval logic by removing ~100 lines of duplicate conditional branching. `isLocalKobold` conditional in `_evaluateRealismForUpcomingGroupSpeaker` removed entirely. `_fireLLMEval` no longer branches on backend type for parameters (always `maxLength: 4000`, `stopSequences: []`, no `banEosToken`/`trimStop` tweaks). All four eval orchestrators use `Future.wait()` for parallel execution. No observable behavior change — KoboldCpp's internal scheduler batches requests safely.

  - Sidebar and Update dialog show clean version strings and correct GitHub links.
  - Added `isNightlyBuild` top-level getter (and kept in CI overwrites) for future-proofing.

2026-06-20 (UTC)
Files changed: installers/windows/setup.iss (converted inline ISPP conditionals for DefaultDirName/DefaultGroupName/OutputBaseFilename and the [Icons] block from the inline {#ifdef ...}...{#else}...{#endif} form to canonical line-based #ifdef/#else/#endif directives; added explanatory comments), .claude/changelog.md (this entry).
Brief reason: Stable Windows releases (release.yml run #213, tag v0.9.9.0.1, which does NOT pass /DPRE_RELEASE) were installing program files into "{localappdata}\Front Porch AI Beta" instead of "{localappdata}\Front Porch AI". Runtime data dir (DB etc.) was correct because that is driven independently by isPreRelease in app_version.dart — confirming the bug was solely in the installer's directory selection. Root cause: setup.iss used the INLINE ISPP conditional form on DefaultDirName, whose branches contain nested braces ({localappdata}, and the inline emit {#MyAppName} which is itself a {# } directive). ISPP's inline brace-matcher mis-parses where the branches end when nested braces are present, so the Beta (PRE_RELEASE) branch leaked through even when PRE_RELEASE was undefined. OutputBaseFilename used the identical inline syntax but its branches were plain text (no nested braces), so it happened to evaluate correctly — which is why stable still shipped Front_Porch_AI_Setup.exe while installing to the wrong dir. Fix: switch all conditionals to line-based #ifdef directives (the documented, unambiguous ISPP form with no inline brace ambiguity). Verified produced installer filenames still match each workflow's copy/rename: release.yml -> Front_Porch_AI_Setup.exe (else), beta-release.yml (/DPRE_RELEASE=1) -> Front_Porch_AI_Beta_Setup.exe, nightly.yml (/DPRE_RELEASE=1 /DNIGHTLY=1) -> Beta name then renamed to Nightly. No Dart code touched (flutter analyze N/A). Cannot run ISCC locally (no Windows/Inno toolchain); change is the canonical ISPP form and is strictly safer than the broken inline form — final confirmation is the next Windows release build.

2026-06-20 (UTC) — silent migration for v0.9.9.0.1 Beta-folder installs
Files changed: installers/windows/setup.iss (stable DefaultDirName now UsePreviousAppDir=no + {code:GetStableInstallDir}; new [Code]: APP_ID const, PrevInstallDirAtStart var, CorrectStableDir/BuggedBetaDir/RecordedInstallDir/GetStableInstallDir/IsRawhideNightlyInstalled helpers, InitializeSetup capture, CurStepChanged nightly-safe cleanup), .claude/changelog.md (this entry).
Brief reason: Follow-up to the inline-conditional fix. Affected stable users (v0.9.9.0.1) have program files in {localappdata}\Front Porch AI Beta and Inno recorded that path under the shared AppId, so a /VERYSILENT auto-update (update_service._launchWindowsInstaller) would silently reinstall back into the Beta folder forever. Fix relocates stable to the correct {localappdata}\Front Porch AI without any user action: UsePreviousAppDir=no + DefaultDirName computed in code (GetStableInstallDir honors a genuine custom path, otherwise forces the correct dir; repairs the bugged Beta path and leaves fresh/correct installs unchanged). CRITICAL constraint from maintainer: Rawhide Nightly AND Beta builds also install into {localappdata}\Front Porch AI Beta (both built with /DPRE_RELEASE) and share the same AppId, so a blind delete would destroy a Nightly user's install. Cleanup of the stray folder runs only when ALL hold: previously-tracked dir (captured in InitializeSetup before the registry is overwritten) == the Beta folder (the bug signature), this install now lives elsewhere, and no Rawhide Nightly is present (detected via its dedicated "Front Porch AI Nightly" Start Menu group in {userprograms}/{commonprograms}). Beta/Nightly installs of this app have {app} == the Beta folder so they skip cleanup entirely. Known accepted edge: a user who has a real BETA (non-Nightly) build in the Beta folder and MANUALLY runs the stable installer would have those beta program files removed — auto-updater channel isolation (update_service ~238) prevents this for normal updates, and user data lives in Documents (FrontPorchAI-Beta), untouched. VERIFICATION: ISCC is Windows-only and could not be run locally; structure validated (balanced #ifdef/#else/#endif 4/4/4, begin/end 10/10, single event funcs, no inline conditionals). The next Windows release CI job compiles the script (fails loudly on any syntax error); a manual Windows smoke test (simulate a Beta-folder stable install, run the new installer, confirm relocation to Front Porch AI + Nightly group preserved) is recommended before cutting the release.

2026-06-20 (UTC) — separate AppId + install folder per channel (stable/Beta/Nightly)
Files changed: installers/windows/setup.iss (rewrite: 3-way channel identity defines ChannelAppId/ChannelSuffix selected by NIGHTLY/PRE_RELEASE; AppId/AppName/DefaultDirName/DefaultGroupName/[Icons]/AppMutex now channel-aware; stable keeps AppId B7E2F8A1-..., Beta=FAAC0B26-5672-4005-A81F-DE7CBA31D327, Nightly=2BBF113C-2BC7-42C3-A654-2BC8478FCDE1; Nightly moved to its own {localappdata}\Front Porch AI Nightly folder; [Code] reworked: APP_ID_STABLE/APP_ID_BETA consts, RecordedInstallDirFor(appId), GetStableInstallDir self-heal kept, BetaAppInstalled + SafeToRemoveBetaFolder unified safe cleanup, removed InitializeSetup/PrevInstallDirAtStart), .claude/changelog.md (this entry).
Brief reason: Root-cause fix approved by maintainer. All 3 channels previously shared ONE hardcoded AppId, so Windows/Inno tracked them as a single app with a single remembered install dir — channels fought over one location and updates clobbered each other (true side-by-side stable+Nightly was never really possible; this also amplified the v0.9.9.0.1 Beta-folder bug). Now each channel has its own AppId and its own folder: stable keeps its AppId (existing installs upgrade in place), Beta/Nightly get fresh AppIds, and Nightly moves out of the shared Beta folder into its own. No workflow changes required — release.yml passes nothing (stable), beta-release.yml /DPRE_RELEASE=1 (Beta), nightly.yml /DPRE_RELEASE=1 /DNIGHTLY=1 (Nightly); output filenames unchanged (Nightly still builds Front_Porch_AI_Beta_Setup.exe and renames). Stable self-heal relocation retained. Cleanup of the stray Beta folder is now a single safe rule (SafeToRemoveBetaFolder): delete only when the Beta folder exists, this install is not the Beta folder, the stable/legacy AppId no longer records the Beta folder as home, and no Beta-channel install owns it — so a real Beta or Nightly is never harmed and the common stable-only leftover is cleaned after relocation. Known accepted minor leftovers (documented, inert, no data loss): a pre-release-only user who never installs stable may keep an orphaned old Beta-folder copy + a stale legacy "Front Porch AI" uninstall entry, since only a later stable install can safely reclaim the shared legacy AppId pointer. All user data stays in Documents (FrontPorchAI / FrontPorchAI-Beta), untouched. VERIFICATION: ISCC is Windows-only, not run locally; validated structure (real directives 4/4/4 nested, begin/end 9/9, single event funcs, channel value mapping). Release CI compiles the script (fails loudly on error); manual Windows smoke test recommended before release: install stable/Beta/Nightly side by side, confirm 3 distinct folders + Start Menu groups + uninstall entries, and confirm a bugged-Beta stable install relocates to Front Porch AI.

2026-06-20 (UTC) — Scene Guests (Lite NPCs) Phase 1: auto chime-in director

Brief reason: After the primary character finishes its reply to a user message in a 1:1 chat that has Scene Guests present, automatically decide which guest(s) should chime in and run their guest turns (each via the existing parity-safe generateGuestTurn, so each appears in its own bubble). New SceneGuestDirector leaf (pure, callback-injected, never imports ChatService) makes the decision: a cheap word-boundary/case-insensitive name-or-nickname heuristic first (guest addressed/referenced -> speak, no LLM), otherwise a token-cheap LLM relevance gate per candidate reusing the existing LlmEvalEngine fire/strip/extractJsonBool surface (no new LLM-firing path) that defaults to NO on empty/parse-failure (KoboldCPP empty-eval gotcha). Guests evaluated in scene order, each speaks at most once per user turn, hard cap of 2 chime-ins/turn (logged truncation via dart:developer log), and later guests' gates see the refreshed transcript tail so they can react to earlier guests. Wired only at the sendMessage level (after the primary _generateResponse + post-turn chip/realism block) and guarded to 1:1 + guests-present + not-generating + not-entrances-in-flight; never called from _generateResponse/generateGuestTurn, so guest turns cannot spawn further chime-ins (plus a defensive _running re-entrancy flag in the leaf). ZERO realism/needs work added (guest turns remain parity-safe). Phase-1 enable flag is an in-memory bool autoChimeEnabled (default ON) with a public setter on ChatService; no persistent setting/UI yet by design. flutter analyze clean on changed files (only the pre-existing unrelated _userMessagesSinceLastEvolution unused_field warning remains). 13 new director tests + existing command-handler tests pass.

2026-06-20 (UTC) — Scene Guests (Lite NPCs) Phase 3: per-guest Character Evolution
Files changed: lib/services/chat_service.dart (maps + 3 private helpers + persist-callback guest branch + save/load blob extension + 3 reset-site mirrors + generateGuestTurn hook), test/services/chat/scene_guest_evolution_test.dart (new, 7 tests), docs/Rawhide.md (user-facing bullet), .claude/changelog.md (this entry).
Brief reason: Scene Guests felt flat because they had no growth. Phase 3 gives each guest the SAME Character Evolution (trait development) as a normal character — no Realism/Needs involvement, session-scoped, and parity-safe. Implementation reuses the existing EvolutionService end-to-end (no parallel evolution path): (1) APPLY — guest evolved text is stored in the shared _evolvedPersonalities/_evolvedScenarios maps keyed by the guest's stable charId, so the existing _getEffectivePersonality/_getEffectiveScenario layering (which already runs for guestSpeaker in _generateResponse) wraps it in the [Character Growth]/[Current Situation] blocks for free; no new APPLY code. (2) TRIGGER — generateGuestTurn now calls _maybeEvolveGuest(guest) after the turn finalizes; it advances a per-guest participation counter (_guestEvolutionCounts) and, on the SAME memorySettings.evolutionInterval used for normal chars, fires the existing _evolutionService.triggerCharacterEvolution(targetCharacter: guest) fire-and-forget. (3) STORAGE — no schema change: the persist callback was generalized so when the target charId is a scene guest (_isSceneGuestCharId) it writes the evolved text into the shared maps + _saveChat instead of the host's session columns; _doSaveChat's existing 1:1 sceneGuests blob now also carries a guestEvolution map ({charId: {count, personality, scenario}}), and _loadSceneGuestsFromSession restores it. (4) SAFETY — guest evolution never runs inside any Realism/Needs path (the guestSpeaker==null post-gen block is untouched), never writes _characterEvolutionCount or the host's session columns, and is cleared via the new _clearSceneGuestEvolution helper mirrored at all three _sceneGuestIds.clear() reset sites + the load site (removes only guest charId entries from the shared maps so nothing leaks across chats). Group chats unaffected (no guests there). Three new private methods added (_isSceneGuestCharId, _maybeEvolveGuest, _clearSceneGuestEvolution) — justified: each is single-purpose and non-overlapping (guest detection by charId / cadence+trigger / reset cleanup) and there was no existing method to extend without conflating host vs guest semantics; no parallel evolution machinery introduced. flutter analyze clean on changed files (only the pre-existing unrelated _userMessagesSinceLastEvolution unused_field warning remains). 7 new tests (blob save/load round-trip incl. no-leak + count-before-text cases, and isLite-card overlay layering) + existing evolution/command/session/director tests pass. Not committed.

2026-06-20 (UTC) — Scene Guests (Lite NPCs) Phase 4: episodic memory (RAG)
Files changed: lib/services/chat_service.dart (generalized _getMemorySourceIds with optional guest param + generalized _maybeEmbedMessages with characterIdOverride + guest embed sibling in generateGuestTurn + retrieval call passes guest: guestSpeaker), lib/services/memory_service.dart (embedMessageWindow dedup scoped to characterId), test/services/chat/scene_guest_memory_test.dart (new, 5 tests), docs/Rawhide.md (user-facing bullet), .claude/changelog.md (this entry).
Brief reason: Scene Guests had no continuity — guest turns were entirely inside the `guestSpeaker == null` realism/needs guard in _generateResponse, so a guest neither embedded to RAG nor retrieved past memories; it always spoke as if it had just arrived. Phase 4 gives each guest its OWN episodic memory by REUSING the existing memory pipeline (no parallel pipeline, no new injection formatter, no new LLM path, ZERO realism/needs). RETRIEVAL: _getMemorySourceIds gained an optional `guest` param — when set it seeds sourceIds with _getCharacterIdFromCard(guest) (the guest's stableGroupId) plus that guest's DB cross-character memorySources, instead of the active (host) character; the existing RAG retrieval block in _generateResponse now calls it with `guest: guestSpeaker`, so on a guest turn the SAME retrieve()/budget/injection format pulls the GUEST's memories and the host's are never injected (and vice versa on a host turn). EMBEDDING: _maybeEmbedMessages gained an optional `characterIdOverride`; generateGuestTurn now fires `_maybeEmbedMessages(characterIdOverride: _getCharacterIdFromCard(guest))` as a sibling after _generateResponse + _maybeEvolveGuest (mirroring the Phase 3 hook), reusing embedMessageWindow to store the just-finished exchange under the guest's id. KEY CONSISTENCY: retrieve key == embed key for a guest — both derive from _getCharacterIdFromCard(guest) == card.stableGroupId. ROUND-TRIP FIX: embedMessageWindow's "already embedded" dedup was scoped only to (positionStart, positionEnd) per session, so once the host embedded window [0-4] the guest's identical range in the same 1:1 session was wrongly skipped (guest memory never stored). Fixed by filtering the existing-range set by the characterId being embedded — host still dedups against its own ranges (host behavior unchanged), and the guest can store its own copy under its own id. PARITY/SAFETY: nothing moved out of the guestSpeaker==null realism/needs guard except the intentional guest retrieval (key swap only) + embed; host 1:1 memory behavior identical; group chats unaffected (no guests). No new private methods — both touched methods were GENERALIZED with optional params (their other call sites, incl. the summary_service getMemorySourceIds callback tear-off, remain valid). flutter analyze clean on changed files (only the pre-existing unrelated _userMessagesSinceLastEvolution unused_field warning remains). 5 new tests (retrieve==embed key, guest key distinct from host, image-less fallback, and the characterId-scoped dedup predicate) + existing memory/guest/evolution tests pass. Not committed.

2026-06-22 (UTC) — Scene Guests (Lite NPCs): manual cast-detection trigger (`/scan`)
Files changed: lib/services/chat/chat_command_handler.dart (new /scan + /detect alias case + runCastScan callback), lib/services/chat_service.dart (new public runCastDetectionNow + consolidated _performCastScan; _maybeRunCastDetection now delegates; handler wiring), test/services/chat/chat_command_handler_test.dart (+4 /scan tests; harness gains runCastScan callback), docs/Rawhide.md (added /scan note to the detection bullet), .claude/changelog.md (this entry).
Brief reason: Cast detection only fired automatically every 4th user turn, and the cadence counter resets on chat load — so there was no way to test it on demand or on an already-open chat where a side character is already repeatedly mentioned. Added a manual `/scan` command (alias `/detect`) that forces an immediate detection pass, bypassing the per-turn cadence. CONSOLIDATION (no parallel path): the automatic path's inline "detect().then(set pending + notify)" block was extracted into one shared private _performCastScan() returning the surfaced DetectedCharacter? (or null); _maybeRunCastDetection() now keeps only the enabled/1:1/active/pending guards + cadence counter and calls _performCastScan() fire-and-forget (unchanged behavior). New public Future<bool> runCastDetectionNow() guards 1:1+active+not-already-pending, zeroes the cadence counter (so the auto scan won't immediately re-fire), awaits _performCastScan(), and returns whether a candidate was surfaced. The handler's /scan case guards active-1:1 (friendly message otherwise), emits a "🔍 Scanning…" status line, awaits runCastScan, and only adds a "No new recurring character was found" line on a miss (on a hit the existing pending-flag → chat_page popup handles surfacing). Detection semantics are otherwise identical to the automatic path — same recent-narration window, same host/user/existing-guest/already-offered filters — so a name previously ignored this session still won't re-surface via /scan (consistent by design; start a fresh chat to re-test a dismissed name). One new private method (_performCastScan, a consolidation that removed the inline duplicate) + one public method; the /scan case is inlined in the switch (no extra handler private method). flutter analyze: No issues found (0 across the project; the unawaited _performCastScan() in the fire-and-forget path is not flagged). 1293 tests pass (incl. 4 new /scan cases: out-of-1:1 reject, miss reports, hit stays silent, /detect alias). flutter build macos --debug green. Not committed.

2026-06-22 (UTC) — Scene Guests (Lite NPCs): regenerating a guest message no longer triggers the Realism Engine
Files changed: lib/services/chat_service.dart (new _sceneGuestForMessage resolver + 6 guards in regenerateLastMessage/swipeMessage), .claude/changelog.md (this entry).
Brief reason: PARITY BUG reported by the user — regenerating (or swiping past the last swipe on) a Scene Guest's message ran the full 1:1 Realism/Needs machinery and regenerated the new swipe spoken as the HOST. regenerateLastMessage gated its realism revert + 4-call re-eval + metadata synthesis + needs-delta computation only on `_realismEnabled && _activeGroup == null`, with NO check for whether the last message was a guest, and called _generateResponse(GenerationMode.normal) with no guestSpeaker — so a guest regen (a) reverted/re-evaluated the active character's bond/trust/emotion/arousal/needs against the guest's swipe, and (b) produced a host-voiced reply instead of the guest. Fixed by adding _sceneGuestForMessage(ChatMessage) — resolves the guest card whose name matches the message sender (null for host/group/system/user; guests are 1:1-only) — and threading its result (regenGuest) through regenerateLastMessage: the realism revert+re-eval block, the 1:1 _pendingRealismMetadata realism_state synthesis block, the post-gen needs-delta computation, and the _restoreRealismStateFromMessage call are all now additionally guarded by `regenGuest == null`, and the regen now calls _generateResponse(GenerationMode.normal, guestSpeaker: regenGuest) so a guest message regenerates as the SAME parity-safe guest turn as the normal path (spoken as the guest, entire realism/needs post-gen block skipped via the existing guestSpeaker==null guard). Calling _generateResponse directly (not generateGuestTurn) is intentional: a regen replaces a swipe, so it must NOT re-advance the guest's evolution counter or re-embed the exchange to RAG (the original turn already did). Also guarded swipeMessage: navigating between a guest message's existing swipes no longer calls _syncRealismStateForSwipe (which would sync the active character's state from guest swipe metadata that carries none). Host-message regen/swipe behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged (all new guards are `&& regenGuest == null` / `if (!isGuestMsg)` additions). One new private method (_sceneGuestForMessage) — justified: correctness/parity resolver with no existing equivalent; reused by both regenerate and swipe. flutter analyze: No issues found. 1293 tests pass. flutter build macos --debug green. Manual: regenerate Vanessa's bubble → new swipe is still Vanessa, host bond/trust/emotion/needs sidebar unchanged, no realism overlay fires. Not committed.

2026-06-22 (UTC) — Scene Guests: fix model identity-confusion + train-wreck guest cards (prompt isolation + scene-grounded generation)
Files changed: lib/services/chat/scene_guest_factory.dart (drop host-scenario inheritance + clear guest scenario + _buildGroundedConcept), lib/services/chat_service.dart (strong guest-turn identity frame + hard host anti-ventriloquism injection + _buildGuestGrounding passed to mint + auto-repair scenario clear in _resolveSceneGuestCards), .claude/changelog.md.
Brief reason: User (on Kimi K2, a strong API model) reported guests deeply confused the model — it thought the guest WAS the host, and the host turn voiced BOTH characters — and that the generated guest card was "a train wreck" with nothing in common with how the character was portrayed in-chat. Five root causes fixed:
(1) SCENARIO BLEED — SceneGuestFactory.mint passed the host's scenario as generateCharacter's `scenario`, which character_gen_service writes onto the card VERBATIM ("use it verbatim"), so the guest's own card literally described the host's story. Now the host scenario is passed only as ephemeral `worldLore` (setting fit) and the guest's card scenario is explicitly cleared (a drop-in guest carries no standalone scenario; identity = description + personality).
(2) WEAK GUEST-TURN FRAME — a guest turn reuses the host's entire transcript, but the only identity switch was a buried one-line author note, so the model conflated guest with host. Replaced with a prominent, explicit frame: "SCENE GUEST TURN. You are now <guest>, NOT <host> and NOT <user>. Everything above was said/done by <host> and <user>; <guest> is a separate person. Reply ONLY as <guest>… do NOT write/speak/narrate anything for <host> or <user>."
(3) HOST DOUBLE-VOICING — the host-turn "guests also present" note softly said "do not fully voice" (the model voiced them anyway → "generated both at once"). Now a hard ban: "Do NOT write any dialogue, actions, or inner thoughts for them — not a single line… never put words or actions on them."
(4) TRAIN-WRECK CARD (the big one) — mint only received name + a one-line concept, so generateCharacter invented a generic character disconnected from the scene. Added ChatService._buildGuestGrounding(name): collects the recent in-chat lines that mention the guest (first-name word-boundary, most-recent 10, capped ~4000 chars), passed as mint(sceneGrounding:). SceneGuestFactory._buildGroundedConcept folds it into the build concept as the dominant signal with an explicit instruction to build ONLY <name> as actually portrayed and ignore details belonging to the narrator/user — so the card now matches the scene's portrayal. Detection-accept path gets this for free (routes through _mintSceneGuest).
(5) EXISTING GUESTS — auto-repair: _resolveSceneGuestCards now clears any non-empty scenario on resolved lite guest cards in-memory every load, so already-minted guests (e.g. Vanessa) self-heal the scenario-bleed without re-creation and with zero risk to their saved portrait (the on-disk scenario is never read for guests; turns build from the resolved card). NOTE: the grounding fix (4) applies to NEWLY minted guests only — an already-generated guest whose *description/personality* is disconnected must be deleted + re-created to benefit (can't regenerate silently on load). All changes are prompt/generation-input only; ZERO Realism/Needs involvement; parity untouched. flutter analyze: No issues found. 1293 tests pass. flutter build macos --debug green. Not committed.

2026-06-22 (UTC) — Scene Guests: harden guest-resolution against concurrent/torn-down DB access (crash hardening)
Files changed: lib/services/chat_service.dart (_resolveSceneGuestCards re-entrancy guard + disposed checks; _onCharacterLibraryChanged defers + guards), .claude/changelog.md.
Brief reason: App crashed with a native SQLite use-after-free (Thread 14: sqlite3 vdbeUnbind/bindText, pc=0x0) on a DartWorker — the signature of the VM/native resources being reinitialized while a DB op was in flight, almost certainly a hot reload/restart triggered by editing .dart files during a live `flutter run -d macos` session. Independent of that tooling cause, the recently-added _onCharacterLibraryChanged listener (re-resolves scene guests on every CharacterRepository change) did synchronous DB reads from inside the repo's notify callback with no re-entrancy guard — a real concurrency risk. Hardened: (1) _resolveSceneGuestCards now guards against overlapping passes (one runs at a time; concurrent requests coalesce into a single trailing re-run via _resolvingSceneGuests/_sceneGuestsResolvePending) so two passes can never race the per-id DB reads or the shared id/card list mutation, and bails on _disposed mid-pass (never touches the DB after teardown); (2) _onCharacterLibraryChanged now skips when _disposed/_guestBusy/no-guests and defers the resolve via scheduleMicrotask so it never starts a read from inside the repository's in-progress write/notify, re-checking guards on the microtask. The deferred listener resolve also won't fight the create/enter flow (which sets _guestBusy and owns its own resolve). NOTE: the disposed guards don't fully prevent a hot-restart-mid-DB-op crash (the old isolate is discarded without a clean dispose) — that's a dev-workflow issue (don't edit Dart against a live flutter run); these guards remove the in-app concurrency risk. flutter analyze clean; 1292 tests pass; flutter build macos --debug green. Not committed.
