Files changed: lib/services/chat_service.dart, lib/services/chat/scene_guest_director.dart, lib/services/chat/cast_detector.dart, lib/services/chat/scene_guest_factory.dart, lib/services/chat/chat_command_handler.dart, lib/ui/pages/chat_page.dart, lib/ui/widgets/character_card_grid.dart, test/services/chat/cast_detector_test.dart (+5), test/services/chat/scene_guest_director_test.dart (+3), .claude/changelog.md.
Brief reason: Ran four parallel hostile reviewers over the whole Scene Guests surface; verified each finding against the code and fixed the real ones.
CONTEXT-TOKEN SAFETY (crash class): added _sceneChanged(token) guard (snapshots _currentSessionId) and threaded it through every fire-and-forget guest op so a chat switch / dispose between awaits can't write the wrong chat: _resolveSceneGuestCards (per-id + pre-writeback), _onCharacterLibraryChanged microtask, _performCastScan (no stale popup in the wrong chat), _addGuestWithStatus (mint/enter/status/portrait), _maybeGenerateGuestPortrait (skip if guest left / chat switched + unique per-invocation temp filename), and the chime-in director (new isContextValid bail between guests). HOST-INVARIANT (parity): (1) _sceneGuestForMessage now keys off _isGuestAuthoredMessage (stable characterId vs the host's), removing the name-fallback that could misclassify a host message as a guest's on a name collision; (2) regenerating a DEPARTED guest's message is now refused (was running the full host realism revert+re-eval against guest-authored text — a real host bond/trust/emotion/needs perturbation); swipe uses the same authoritative check; (3) loadSession (history switch) now resets + reloads scene-guest state for 1:1 (was leaking the previous session's guests into and contaminating the loaded session's blob); (4) STOPPED mutating the shared library card — the scenario auto-repair wrote card.scenario='' on the repo's live reference (corrupting a /join'd character for when it's a host); the guest scenario is now blanked ONLY in the prompt at guest-turn time (still self-heals legacy guests, preserves real scenarios); (5) continueGeneration + impersonateUser now guard _guestBusy.
GENERATION/DETECTION: cast_detector JSON parse switched from greedy \{.*\} (died on trailing prose / two objects) to a balanced brace-scan _firstJsonObject; _collides is token-aware (≥3-char non-title shared token) so "Ed" no longer suppresses "Fred"/"Ned" and "Sam"≠"Samuel", while "Mara"/"Mara Vance" still collide; cast scan reads HOST-authored narration only (excludes guest messages); _buildGuestGrounding skips grounding when the guest's first name overlaps the host/user (host-bleed); director nickname heuristic ignores title first-tokens ("Major Tom" no longer fires on "major"); factory safeName falls back to 'guest' for non-Latin/symbol names.
UX/MISC: _addGuestWithStatus rejects a duplicate guest name and surfaces "busy" instead of silently dropping; _maybeEvolveGuest persists the bumped participation count on non-evolving turns; a deleted/departed guest's old bubble now shows a placeholder avatar (not the host's face); /exit with an ambiguous substring asks for the full name instead of removing the first match; Scene Guests get a "Guest" badge in the library grid (uses the previously-dead isLite getter; they stay visible so they remain deletable / known-cast). ## 2026-06-23 — Fix the per-turn realism speaker resolver (pin the actual speaker)
- Files: lib/services/chat_service.dart (new `_turnSpeakerIdForRealism` field), lib/services/chat/chat_service_generation.dart (set pin after speaker pick + clear in a new finally on _generateResponse's outer try), lib/services/chat/chat_service_group_realism_helpers.dart (`_getCurrentSpeakerIdForRealism` prefers the pin), test/services/chat/turn_speaker_resolver_test.dart (NEW, 6 tests).
- Reason: `_getCurrentSpeakerIdForRealism()` derived "who's speaking now" from `GroupTurnManager.nextSpeaker` — but that's the UPCOMING speaker: after a round-robin pick the turn pointer has already advanced (so during the current speaker's turn it points at the NEXT member), and for random turn order it's null (speaker chosen at pick time) so the resolver fell back to `_groupCharacters.first` (always the primary). This resolver feeds ALL prompt-injection builders (needs/relationship/emotion/nsfw/realism_state), realism_verification, affection decay (relationship_service:683), tickDecay (needs_simulation:279), the needs-impact evaluator, and reprocess. Net effect: in round-robin each character's PROMPT was injected with the OTHER member's needs/relationship/mood, and in random turn order decay/affection always hit the primary. Fix: pin the speaker the moment they're picked in `_generateResponse` (`_turnSpeakerIdForRealism = (_activeGroup != null && guestSpeaker == null) ? id : null`) and clear it in a `finally` on the method's outer try so it can't leak into the pre-pick window (`_applyMoodDecay`, which runs in sendMessage BEFORE _generateResponse and must keep its prior nextCharacter behaviour). The resolver prefers the pin when set + still in roster, else the old nextCharacter→first fallback. Regen already pins via `_groupManager.setNextSpeaker(originalSpeaker)` (reprocess:425) before _generateResponse, so the pin follows the regenerated member. 1:1 unaffected (resolver early-returns before the group branch).
- Safeguards (user opted into "do it properly"): the new chip helper from the prior fix uses the per-message baseline so it was already immune; this fix corrects the prompt-injection + decay keying. Verified: flutter analyze clean (full project); 377/377 chat tests + 6 new resolver tests green; ADVERSARIAL multi-agent review (4 lenses: pin lifecycle/leaks, regen, prompt-injection behavior correctness, 1:1 parity/set-condition; each finding independently refuted) returned 0 confirmed issues. No re-entrancy (the `_isGenerating` guard prevents nested _generateResponse, so the inner finally can't clear an outer turn's pin).

## 2026-06-23 — Native KoboldCpp: ban EOS on structured instruction calls (fixes empty char-gen + silent eval failures)
- Files: lib/services/chargen/character_gen_llm.dart (banEosToken now also true when `_llmService is KoboldService && isJsonMode`), lib/services/chat/fact_extraction.dart (banEosToken `isThinkingModel && getIsLocal()` → `getIsLocal()`; doc-comment updated), lib/services/chat/expression_classifier.dart (banEosToken `isThinkingModel` → `isThinkingModel || llmService is KoboldService`; added `kobold_service.dart` import).
- Reason: User reported AI character creation returning 0–8 chars then stopping on native KoboldCpp (Skyfall-31B Q8), while oMLX worked with the same model. Root cause is NOT the `<END>` stop strings (the prompt never contains them) — it's that KoboldCpp's raw text-completion endpoint (`/api/extra/generate/stream`) applies no instruct template, so an instruct-tuned GGUF treats the bare instruction prompt as a finished document and emits EOS immediately (`len=0`). oMLX dodges this because its `/chat/completions` path wraps the prompt in the model's template server-side. The codebase already documents + works around this for realism evals (`llm_eval_engine.dart:291` `banEosToken: effectiveIsLocal`, comment "thinking prefill otherwise returns len=0"), but the workaround was applied inconsistently: char-gen only banned EOS when reasoning was on, fact-extraction only for local *thinking* models, expression-classifier only for thinking models. So on a non-thinking local model, char-gen failed loudly and fact-extraction/emotion-reclassification failed *silently* (fell back to defaults). This is the "deeper base issue" the user intuited; char-gen was just the loudest symptom.
- Scope (Tier 1 — consistent EOS band-aid, only where SAFE): applied to the three instruction callers that have a reliable non-EOS stop, so banning EOS can't run away — char-gen JSON mode (balanced-brace checker ends the stream at object close), fact-extraction (`]` stop), expression-classifier (`}` stop, maxLength 32). Deliberately NOT applied to prose/no-stop callers where banning EOS would generate to maxLength: char-gen greetings (prose, `<END>` only), summary (prose, continuation-framed — likely already fine), objective tasks/completion (empty stops, maxLen 2000), evolution (empty stops, maxLen ≤16384). image_prompt_builder has a `\n\n` stop (borderline-safe) and was left out of this pass. Those prose paths need Tier 2 (route native-kobold instruction calls through KoboldCpp's `/v1/chat/completions` so the GGUF template is applied, then delete the EOS band-aids).
- Parity: EOS flag is keyed on backend locality (`is KoboldService` / `getIsLocal()`), identical in 1:1 and group — expression-classifier and fact-extraction run per-character the same way in both modes, so Realism/Needs parity is preserved. No group-vs-1:1 divergence introduced.
- Hygiene: no new methods; one import added (used); comments updated to explain the local-EOS rationale; doc-comment in fact_extraction corrected. flutter analyze clean on all three changed files. NOT yet committed/pushed — user is smoke-testing native KoboldCpp first; greetings expected to still return empty until Tier 2.
- Commit: (pending — local only, awaiting smoke test)

## 2026-06-23 — Image Studio: fix reversed typing in the custom prompt / negative-prompt fields
- Files: lib/ui/image_studio/prompt_workspace.dart (converted PromptWorkspace from StatelessWidget to StatefulWidget with persistent controllers).
- Reason: User reported that typing in the Image Studio "Prompt (editable before generation)" and "Negative prompt (for this generation)" fields inserted each character at the START, producing a backwards prompt (e.g. "sdrawkcab si tpmorp siht"). Root cause: both TextFields built `controller: TextEditingController(text: prompt/negative)` inline in `build()`, so a brand-new controller was created on every rebuild. Each keystroke → onChanged → parent setState → rebuild → fresh controller whose selection defaults to a collapsed caret at offset 0 → the next character inserts at the front. (It also leaked an undisposed controller per rebuild.) A stale comment even rationalized the recreate-per-build pattern as avoiding "cursor-jump fights"; that reasoning was wrong — recreating an editable field's controller every build is what causes the caret reset.
- Fix: PromptWorkspace now owns two persistent `TextEditingController`s created once in `initState`, disposed in `dispose`. `didUpdateWidget` pushes parent changes into the controllers ONLY when they differ from the field's current text — i.e. an external rewrite via "Craft / Refresh with LLM", not the user's own typing (where widget.prompt already mirrors the controller) — and on such an external swap sets the caret to the end. The parent already keys it with a stable `const ValueKey('workspace')` inside an AnimatedSwitcher and keeps `view == 'workspace'` while typing, so the State persists across keystroke rebuilds (didUpdateWidget fires, not initState) and the fix holds. Public constructor/API unchanged, so the call site in image_studio.dart needs no edits.
- Hygiene: no new helper methods (only the standard StatefulWidget lifecycle overrides initState/didUpdateWidget/dispose); deleted the per-build controller anti-pattern and the misleading comment. File 348 → 393 lines (under the 500 cap). flutter analyze clean on both prompt_workspace.dart and the parent image_studio.dart; dart format reports no changes.
- Commit: (pending — awaiting user smoke test)

## 2026-06-23 — Fix GGUF arch-parser RangeError spam (pre-existing; exposed by working Kobold gen)
- Files: lib/utils/gguf_parser.dart (getModelArchitectureInfo value switch wrapped in try/break), lib/services/model_manager.dart (negative cache for unparseable files).
- Reason: Console spammed with "Failed to parse GGUF architecture info: RangeError (byteOffset): ... 4194307" while using the (now working) Kobold chat backend. Two pre-existing bugs: (1) getModelArchitectureInfo reads only the first 4 MB of the GGUF then walks the metadata, but its value-read switch has NO per-value bounds checks (unlike the sibling getKvCacheBytesPerToken, despite a comment claiming they're "kept in sync") — the big tokenizer.ggml.tokens array on large-vocab models (Skyfall-31B) runs past 4 MB and throws RangeError; (2) model_manager only cached SUCCESSFUL parses, so every failed parse re-ran. My chat-door fix made generation stream tokens → frequent notifyListeners → settings/UI rebuilds re-calling the parser → the failure repeated on a loop. Exposed by, not caused by, the refactor.
- Fix: (1) wrap the value switch in try/catch and break the metadata loop on overflow — the architecture keys (block_count/head_count/embedding_length) appear before the tokenizer data, so `meta` already holds them and the post-loop code returns valid GGUFModelInfo instead of throwing (so parsing now SUCCEEDS for these models, improving VRAM/layer estimates too); (2) negative-cache files that yield null in model_manager so they're parsed once, not every frame.
- Verification: flutter analyze clean; dart format clean; test/utils green (no dedicated gguf test exists). Isolated to gguf_parser + model_manager (untouched by the unify refactor) — separately committable.
- Commit: (pending)

## 2026-06-24 — ci(nightly/macOS): resilient codesign + self-diagnosing notarization (Rawhide-only, fixes intermittent staple failures)
- Files: .github/workflows/nightly.yml (Code Sign macOS App step + Notarize step).
- Reason: Rawhide macOS nightly intermittently failed notarization (status Invalid → "Could not find base64 ticket… Error 65"), while identical-signing builds incl. the v0.9.9.1.3 release passed. Diagnosed: `codesign --timestamp` runs 8-way parallel over thousands of PyInstaller Mach-O files; each --timestamp is a network call to Apple's timestamp server, which throttles under the burst. Failures were swallowed by `|| true`, so a binary could ship without a secure timestamp → Apple rejects the whole .pkg as Invalid (intermittently). Cert/credentials/Apple-service ruled out (the release notarized fine, same cert/account).
- Fix (signing): every codesign now RETRIES (until-loop, up to 4x with backoff) so a throttled timestamp self-heals; a genuine failure now FAILS the build at the signing step naming the file (replaced `…| grep -v …|| true` with retry + per-file log shown only on failure; find targets wrapped `{ … || true; }` so a missing dir doesn't fail the pipe but a real codesign failure does); added a `codesign --verify --deep --strict` gate before notarization so an unsigned/invalid nested binary fails HERE with the path, not as a mystery Invalid later.
- Fix (notarize): `notarytool submit --wait` exits 0 even on Invalid (the old `|| {exit 1}` never caught it → it proceeded to staple and died), so now the status is parsed explicitly and on anything but Accepted, `notarytool log <id>` is fetched + printed — future failures are self-diagnosing in CI.
- Scope: Rawhide-only per plan — validate via a manual Rawhide build, then propagate to main's nightly.yml + release.yml (which share this signing code). Validated: YAML parses, signing-step `bash -n` parses; runtime only testable on the macOS runner.
- Commit: (this commit)

## 2026-06-24 — ci(nightly/macOS): fix "bundle format is ambiguous" on PyInstaller framework main binaries
- Files: .github/workflows/nightly.yml (framework pass + catch-all pass).
- Reason: the previous commit's fail-loud signing surfaced the REAL intermittent-notarization cause (previously swallowed by `|| true`): the framework pass tried to `codesign` a framework's MAIN binary as a loose file — e.g. dt_grpc_client/_internal/Python.framework/Python — which codesign refuses with "bundle format is ambiguous (could be app or framework)". That left the binary improperly signed → Apple rejected the .pkg as Invalid. (dt_grpc_client = the Draw Things gRPC sidecar, a newer PyInstaller bundle, which is why it surfaced now.)
- Fix: a framework's main binary must be signed via the framework BUNDLE, not the inner file. Framework pass now skips the framework's own main binary in the inner per-file loop (basename == framework basename); the existing `codesign "$fw"` bundle sign on the next line handles it. Catch-all pass excludes `*.framework/*` so it can't re-hit the same inner binary (frameworks are fully handled by the framework pass).
- Validated: YAML parses, signing-step bash -n parses. Rawhide-only; re-test via manual Rawhide build.
- Commit: (this commit)

## 2026-06-24 — ci(nightly/macOS): retry-then-TOLERATE signing (revise — don't fail on the harmless PyInstaller framework quirk)

So Apple tolerates it (warning, not rejection); failing on it breaks a build Apple accepts.

## 2026-06-25 (UTC) — fix(installer): Windows Nightly auto-update loop (forked install instead of upgrading in place)
- Files: lib/services/update_service.dart, installers/windows/setup.iss, docs/Rawhide.md, .claude/changelog.md (this entry).
- PRIMARY FIX (find + honor the user's custom install dir, all channels, permanent): UpdateService._launchWindowsInstaller now passes /DIR=<current install dir> to the Inno installer, where the dir is File(Platform.resolvedExecutable).parent.path (a .installed-marked install means resolvedExecutable is "<installDir>\front_porch_ai.exe", so its parent is the exact folder the user chose — default OR a custom drive/path). Inno's /DIR overrides DefaultDirName and the previous-app-dir and works with /VERYSILENT (verified against jrsoftware.org/ishelp setupcmdline). This makes every auto-update install IN PLACE on top of the running build, regardless of location or AppId — which structurally eliminates the entire "silent update forks a copy into the default dir" failure mode (the Nightly loop) for Stable/Beta/Nightly alike, and is the only safe way to honor a CUSTOM dir: the running app is the sole component that authoritatively knows where it lives. Deliberately NOT done: rediscovering a custom dir from the registry inside the installer — the pre-split AppId was shared with Stable/Beta, so a registry guess could install Nightly on top of a Stable install (an unrecoverable mistake), which is exactly why the truth is sourced from the running app instead. Defensive: a trailing backslash is stripped from the dir so the quoted /DIR value can't be malformed (install dirs never end in a separator in practice). Dart Process.start quotes args containing spaces on Windows, so "Front Porch AI Nightly"-style paths pass through correctly.
- Reason: Discord report — Nightly "auto-installs into appdata/local with no folder choice" AND "keeps asking to update over and over but never installs the latest one." Root cause traced to the AppId split on 2026-06-20 (commit 0a7a04e), which gave the Nightly channel a brand-new Inno AppId ({2BBF113C-…}) plus a dedicated folder. Pre-split Nightly shared the legacy AppId ({B7E2F8A1-…}) and installed into "{localappdata}\Front Porch AI Beta". The in-app updater has ALWAYS run the installer with /VERYSILENT (since f57ac8e). For an existing (pre-split) Nightly user, the new installer's AppId has no recorded path in Windows, so /VERYSILENT treats it as a FRESH install and drops a second copy into "{localappdata}\Front Porch AI Nightly" while the running build (old AppId, in the Beta folder) is never touched. The running app keeps reporting the old version → the GitHub check keeps finding the new nightly → endless update loop; and because it's silent, the user never sees a directory page (hence "no folder choice" + "lands in appdata/local").
- Fix (Option A — adopt the existing install dir, mirroring the proven stable GetStableInstallDir self-heal): Nightly's DefaultDirName now routes through a new GetNightlyInstallDir [Code] routine, with UsePreviousAppDir=no for Nightly so the code FULLY owns the directory (exactly like stable). UsePreviousAppDir=no is the critical correctness point: a user who is ALREADY looping has already forked at least one copy into the dedicated "...\Front Porch AI Nightly" folder, so the new Nightly AppId already records that path. With the Inno default (UsePreviousAppDir=yes) the recorded dedicated-folder path would win and bypass DefaultDirName/code entirely — reinstalling to the dedicated folder forever while the running build in the Beta folder is never replaced (loop NOT healed for exactly the people who have it). With =no, GetNightlyInstallDir decides every time: (1) HEAL — if a pre-split Nightly is still in the Beta folder, return the Beta folder so the silent update overwrites the RUNNING build in place (works even post-fork); (2) NO-CLOBBER GUARD — the heal fires only when Nightly's dedicated Start Menu group exists (IsRawhideNightlyInstalled) AND front_porch_ai.exe is in the Beta folder AND the Beta AppId ({FAAC0B26}) does NOT record the Beta folder, so a genuine Beta install (which owns that folder under the Beta AppId) is never adopted/clobbered even when a Nightly also exists; (3) otherwise honor the recorded Nightly-AppId path (preserves a user-chosen custom folder) and fall back to the dedicated folder for fresh installs. The [Setup] dir conditional was restructured from a flat #ifdef PRE_RELEASE into #ifdef NIGHTLY / #else #ifdef PRE_RELEASE (Beta) / #else (stable) so Nightly and Beta — which both build with PRE_RELEASE — take different dir logic. Added APP_ID_NIGHTLY const. Existing stable self-heal (GetStableInstallDir) and SafeToRemoveBetaFolder are unchanged and already protect a migrated Nightly squatting in the Beta folder (SafeToRemoveBetaFolder requires `not IsRawhideNightlyInstalled()`).
- Directory choice preserved: DisableDirPage is still unset (Inno default 'auto'), so every FRESH install of any channel shows the Select Destination Location page; only in-place upgrades and /VERYSILENT auto-updates skip it. (With UsePreviousAppDir=no, interactive Nightly upgrades will also show the page, defaulting to the resolved folder — harmless and arguably clearer.) No change to the in-app updater (still /VERYSILENT) — the installer now does the right thing on its own.
- Why both layers (the /DIR primary fix AND the setup.iss heal): version skew. The /DIR fix lives in the updater (Dart), so it only takes effect once a user is running a build that CONTAINS it. Users who are looping right now are running OLD builds whose updater can't pass /DIR, so the installer must still rescue them. The setup.iss GetNightlyInstallDir heal bridges the common case — a pre-split Nightly in the default "...\Front Porch AI Beta" folder — by installing over it in place, which lands them on a /DIR-enabled build; from then on /DIR keeps every update in place. Together: /DIR = never happens again for anyone on a fixed build (incl. custom dirs); the heal = rescue the already-stuck common case.
- New code: 1 Inno Pascal function (GetNightlyInstallDir) + 1 const (APP_ID_NIGHTLY) in setup.iss; ~10 lines in _launchWindowsInstaller (compute dir + /DIR arg) reusing dart:io File/Platform already imported. No methods deleted (none became dead); no new Dart methods (edit is inside the existing _launchWindowsInstaller).
- Residual edge (documented, not auto-fixed by design): a user currently running an OLD build installed to a CUSTOM folder who ALSO already forked an AppData copy cannot be auto-bridged to that custom folder by the installer — the only registry trace of the custom dir is the Stable/Beta-shared legacy AppId, and adopting it could clobber a real Stable install, which we refuse to risk. Such a user self-heals the moment they run a fixed build (then /DIR honors their folder forever), or can reinstall via the wizard's directory page / uninstall the duplicate via Apps & Settings. Their chats/data are unaffected (stored under Documents, not the install folder). Also unchanged: a healed Nightly that stays in the Beta folder would re-collide if a real Beta is later installed there — pre-existing pre-split behavior, not a regression.
- Verification: no local Flutter/Dart SDK in this env, so flutter analyze/build are gated on CI; the Dart edit was manually reviewed (no new imports, File/Platform from dart:io already imported, no unused vars, runs only on the Windows install path). setup.iss is Windows-only (ISCC) and compiled by release/nightly CI; structure validated locally (balanced #ifdef/#else/#endif 5/5/5, single begin/end, deps declared before use, {code:} resolved at runtime). REQUIRES a manual Windows smoke test before release: (a) custom-dir install (e.g. D:\…) → auto-update lands back in D:\…, no AppData copy; (b) currently-looping pre-split Nightly in the default Beta folder → update installs over it in place, loop gone; (c) real Beta present alongside a Nightly → Beta folder never adopted/clobbered; (d) Stable custom-dir → still updates in place.

## 2026-06-25 — Web UI rewrite Phase 4: Tailscale / ngrok / TLS (Rawhide)
- Files (NEW): lib/services/web/tunnels/{tailscale_provider,ngrok_provider,tunnel_manager}.dart, lib/services/web/util/self_signed_cert.dart, lib/services/web/routes/remote_routes.dart, test/services/web/tunnels_test.dart. Modified: web_server_deps.dart (+tunnelManager), server_bootstrap.dart (register remote routes), web_server_host.dart (create TunnelManager from bind port; optional self-signed TLS for LAN; dispose), storage/settings/web_server_settings.dart (+ngrokAuthToken, +tlsSelfSigned).
- Reason: First-class remote access (a headline user ask). TailscaleProvider detects an installed tailscale, parses `status --json` (MagicDNS name, 100.x IP, BackendState) and uses `tailscale serve` so the daemon terminates TLS with a publicly-trusted *.ts.net cert (no cert/renewal code on our side; we trust X-Forwarded-Proto from loopback). NgrokProvider detects/​spawns the agent and reads the public https URL from the local :4040 API (robust vs stdout scraping). TunnelManager aggregates both into one {type,url,secure,status} surface for the Flutter settings + React Remote Access page. SelfSignedCert (basic_utils, RSA keygen in an isolate, cached PEMs) is the ENCRYPTION-ONLY LAN fallback — documented in code + the status payload that browsers warn on it and it is not a true secure context (Tailscale/ngrok/localhost are the PWA-capable paths). Binaries are detected, never bundled.
- Endpoints: GET /api/remote/status, POST /api/remote/tailscale {enable}, POST /api/remote/ngrok {enable, authToken?}.

## 2026-06-25 — Web server: drop self-signed TLS; direct binds are plain HTTP (Rawhide)
- Files: DELETED lib/services/web/util/self_signed_cert.dart; lib/services/web/web_server_host.dart (removed _buildTlsContext + securityContext bind + self_signed_cert/path imports — always plain http now); lib/services/storage/settings/web_server_settings.dart (removed webServerTlsSelfSigned setting); pubspec.yaml (removed basic_utils dep); test/services/web/tunnels_test.dart (removed the SelfSignedCert test group + dart:io/self_signed imports).
- Reason: A self-signed cert triggers the browser's full-page "not secure / not trusted" warning and forces the user to click through — worse UX than plain HTTP, and it still isn't a true secure context unless the cert is manually trusted. So direct binds (localhost and LAN IPs, desktop and mobile browsers) now serve plain HTTP with no cert prompt. Real, warning-free HTTPS comes ONLY from a trusted external terminator — Tailscale `serve` (publicly-trusted *.ts.net cert) or ngrok — over which our server still stays plain http on loopback. localhost remains a secure context over http by spec.
- Verification: flutter analyze clean (only the pre-existing chat_service.dart:8005 warning); test/services/web 35/35 pass; no remaining self-signed/TLS references in lib or test.

- Files: web_ui/src/pages/ChatPage.tsx, web_ui/src/components/MessageContent.tsx, assets/web_app/** (rebuilt bundle)
- Reason: The chat flickered/"reloaded" during generation and realism. ## 2026-07-03 — Fix Windows 11 "app opens as an unreachable taskbar icon" (issue #78)
- **Files**: lib/main.dart (window restore + save paths only).
- **Root cause**: When the app was closed while the window was MINIMIZED on Windows, `windowManager.isMaximized()` returns false, so onWindowClose took the else branch and saved `windowManager.getPosition()` — which for a minimized Win32 window is the classic minimized sentinel (~ -32000, -32000). That poisoned `window_x`/`window_y`. On the next launch the restore code called `setBounds(Rect.fromLTWH(-32000, -32000, w, h))`, stranding the window far off-screen: it showed only as a taskbar icon that WIN+arrow / ALT+Enter could not recover. Because Windows SharedPreferences lives in %APPDATA%\Roaming (outside the app's data folders), uninstalling + deleting the FrontPorchAI folders did NOT clear the poisoned prefs — so it survived a full reinstall, exactly as the reporter described.
- **Fix (two parts)**: (1) Save side — onWindowClose now also checks `isMinimized()` and treats minimized like maximized, persisting the tracked non-minimized `_normal*` bounds instead of the bogus live rect, so the sentinel is never written. (2) Restore side — new top-level `_windowBoundsVisible(Rect)` validates the saved rect against the connected displays (via screen_retriever, already a transitive dep of window_manager) before `setBounds`; if no grabbable chunk overlaps any display's visible area (minimized sentinel, or a since-unplugged monitor), we skip the restore and fall through to the centered WindowOptions default. This self-heals already-poisoned installs without the user editing the registry/prefs. The helper cheaply rejects the sentinel first and falls back to trusting saved bounds if display enumeration throws pre-runApp.
- **Cross-platform**: guard is a no-op on healthy installs on all three desktop OSes; the sentinel/off-screen path is Windows-specific but the visibility check is generically correct on macOS/Linux too (rescues windows stranded by a disconnected monitor).
- **Verified**: flutter analyze lib/main.dart — 0 issues.

## 2026-07-03 — Needs deltas from the last message could be lost on app close (no flush-on-exit)
- **Files**: lib/services/chat/chat_service_session_state.dart (new public `flushPendingSaves()`), lib/main.dart (call it in `onWindowClose` before backend teardown/exit).
- **Symptom (user-reported, intermittent)**: after a character reply, closing and reopening the app would "periodically" show the sidebar Needs levels reverted — the post-generation Needs deltas from the last message (the chips) didn't stick, even though the message and its chip were still there.
- **Root cause**: the Needs vector reaches the DB only through `_saveChat()` → `_doSaveChat()`, and the post-impact vector's durable write is the last thing a turn does. Many `_saveChat()` calls are fire-and-forget (`unawaited`, `Future.microtask`, non-awaited UI setters), so the write carrying the last turn's post-impact vector could still be queued or mid-commit when the user closed. `onWindowClose` saved window prefs, stopped backends, then `exit(0)`/`windowManager.destroy()` **without waiting for any pending save** — killing that write. The message text survived from an earlier save (taken pre-impact, before deltas applied), so on reopen the message + chip were present but the sidebar levels reflected the pre-message state. Intermittent purely by close timing → "periodically."
- **Fix**: `flushPendingSaves()` awaits `_saveChat()`, which drains the whole `_saveChain` (nothing in flight is dropped) and writes the live in-memory state one final time — bounded/fast, no-ops when there's no session/messages. `onWindowClose` now awaits it first thing in cleanup, so close waits for every pending write (and any mid-commit transaction) to land before the process dies.
- **Scope/parity**: no changes to per-turn Realism/Needs logic; reuses the single `_saveChat` path (handles 1:1 and group identically), so 1:1-vs-group parity is untouched. One new *public* method (no existing public flush), one call site; no dead code introduced. SIGINT/SIGTERM (terminal Ctrl-C / OS shutdown) keep their deliberate "exit immediately" behavior — the normal user-close path is `onWindowClose`.
- **Verified**: full `flutter analyze` — 0 issues.

## 2026-07-04 — The Journal wrote recaps but almost never memory cards (prompt too timid)
- **Files**: lib/services/chat/journal_prompt.dart (rules block + both closing sections), docs/Rawhide.md (user-facing note).
- **Symptom (user-reported)**: after chatting with several characters, no journal entries ever appeared. Confirmed against the live DB: of 95 chats, 28 had a "Where we are" recap but only 1 (an exceptionally intense chat) had memory cards — the maintenance pass was running and succeeding (cursor advancing, recap written) yet emitting zero add_memory ops in nearly every chat.
- **Root cause**: prompt-balance issue, not a bug. The pass asks the model to (a) write a recap — framed as mandatory ("Finish with exactly one write_recap call") — and (b) add memory cards — framed as heavily optional and filtered ("Only add durable memories… Skip small talk"). Models (local and, per user, capable OpenRouter models alike) follow the explicit mandatory instruction and skip the discretionary one unless the scene is unmistakably dramatic. Parsing, applier, storage, and UI are all correct; the model simply wasn't emitting adds.
- **Fix**: rebalanced the shared prompt body (both XML and tool transports read it, so 1:1/group parity is structural). The "only add durable / skip small talk" rule became "Capture what mattered: add a memory for each promise made, thing learned about $user, relationship shift, or moment that stood out… when any line is annotated, write at least one memory for it… do not finish a pass with no new memory when something worth remembering happened" (keeps a small-talk guard against spam). Both closings now lead with memories, then the recap ("Add your memories first with add_memory, then finish with… write_recap" / "Write your <memory> tags first, then end with… <recap>").
- **Scope/parity**: prompt text only; no schema, storage, or logic change. Shared body → 1:1 and group identical. No new methods, no dead code.
- **Verified**: flutter analyze on journal_prompt.dart — 0 issues; journal_test.dart + journal_physics_test.dart — 49/49 pass. NOT yet observed against a live OpenRouter pass (requires the running app + the user's key) — pending the user chatting and confirming cards now appear.

## 2026-07-04 — The REAL cause: journal entries missing on "thinking" models (reasoning starved the tool call)
- **Files**: lib/services/chat/llm_eval_engine.dart (shared text-eval params), lib/services/chat_service.dart (journal tool-eval params) — both now pass `reasoningMaxTokens: 0` alongside `reasoningEnabled: false`. docs/Rawhide.md updated.
- **Follow-up to the same-day prompt-balance fix**: after strengthening the journal prompt, the user (on Nano-GPT, model `moonshotai/kimi-k2.6:thinking`) still saw entries only intermittently — regenerating 2–3× to get any cards.
- **Diagnosis (verified live against the user's own backend)**: `OpenRouterService._chatPayload` only emits the reasoning-disable block when `params.reasoningEnabled || params.reasoningMaxTokens != null`. The eval params set `reasoningEnabled: false` but left `reasoningMaxTokens` null, so **no reasoning field was sent at all** → a ":thinking" model keeps reasoning ON for the journal pass. Reproduced the exact payloads against the live API: THINKING ON burned ~5,586 chars (~1,300 tokens) of hidden reasoning, completion 1,630 tokens, and emitted FEWER tool calls (4); THINKING OFF burned 0 reasoning, completion 343 tokens, emitted MORE tool calls (10). On a real chat (large window + existing cards) the reasoning can consume the whole 4,000-token budget and truncate the response before any tool call is written → zero cards. Intermittent by how long the model happened to think → "had to regen twice." The raw tool-call parsing (`parseOpenAiToolResponse` + `parseJournalToolCalls`) was confirmed correct — not the culprit.
- **Fix**: set `reasoningMaxTokens: 0` in both eval param builders → `_chatPayload` now sends `reasoning: {enabled:false, max_tokens:0, exclude:true}` (the "strongest disable signal" its own comment describes, intended exactly for Kimi K2.6). Applies to the journal tool call AND all shared text evals (Realism etc.), which are structured-extraction calls that should never reason — faster, cheaper, more reliable on thinking models. Local KoboldCpp unaffected (`_chatPayload` is the remote path). Same code path for 1:1 and group → Realism/Needs parity preserved; no simulation logic touched.
- **Verified**: flutter analyze (3 changed files) 0 issues; journal_test.dart + journal_physics_test.dart 49/49 pass; live A/B against Nano-GPT/Kimi (numbers above) confirms thinking-off reliably returns the tool calls the app needs.

## 2026-07-06 — Fix: action snackbars (Undo/OK/View) never auto-dismissed

- **Files:** lib/ui/pages/chat_page.dart (two SnackBars: the `/exit`|`/leave` "X left the scene" UNDO toast + the TTS-error "OK" toast — both gain `persist: false`), lib/ui/pages/repository/stoop_inbox_bell.dart (the "New message from a moderator" View toast gains `persist: false`), docs/Rawhide.md (user-facing bullet).
- **Reason:** A Discord user reported the "Mark left the scene" UNDO snackbar staying on screen forever. Root cause is a Flutter framework behavior (confirmed in the pinned SDK 3.41.5): `SnackBar`'s new `persist` field **defaults to `action != null`** (snack_bar.dart:303 `persist = persist ?? action != null`). In scaffold.dart the auto-dismiss `Timer(snackBar.duration, …)` still fires, but its body early-returns when `snackBar.persist` is true (`if (snackBar.persist) return;`), so the toast never hides. Every snackbar in the app that has a `SnackBarAction` and doesn't pass `persist:false` was therefore stuck regardless of its `duration`. There are only three such call sites (grep `SnackBarAction` → 2 files); all three clearly intend to be transient (each sets or defaults a duration), so all three now pass `persist:false`.
- **Verification:** Reproduced the bug and validated the fix with a throwaway widget-test probe (since removed): a vanilla 8s `SnackBar` **with** an action never dismissed across 20s of pumping; the identical snackbar **without** an action dismissed at 8.6s; adding `persist:false` to the action snackbar restored dismissal at 8.6s. `flutter analyze` on both changed files — No issues found. `dart fix --dry-run` — Nothing to fix. Web parity: unaffected — the web UI shows `/exit` status via a state-driven cast banner (CastBar.tsx `guestStatus`), not a Flutter SnackBar, so it doesn't share the `persist` default (no web-side change needed).
- **Commit:** (this change — Rawhide)

## 2026-07-06 — Fix: characters never climaxed autonomously at peak lust (needed an OOC nudge)

- **Files:** lib/services/chat/prompt_injection/nsfw_injection.dart (the >80 "peak arousal" branch of `buildNsfwCooldownInjection`), test/services/chat/prompt_injection_test.dart (+1 regression test).
- **Reason:** A user reported that a character with Lust at/near 100, even mid-scene in active sexual contact, would edge indefinitely and never actually finish unless the user broke immersion with an `OOC:` "finish the action" prompt. Root cause: at the peak arousal tier the injected Physical-State note contained an explicit hard prohibition — *"Do NOT write orgasm or post-orgasm behavior unless the physical activity in the scene has naturally built to that point through {{user}}'s direct actions … still in the moment, not past it."* Models read this as a blanket ban on autonomous release, so the character stayed stuck on the edge. It also created a stuck state loop: the post-gen climax detector (`is_climax` in needs_impact_evaluator → `onClimax` → refractory) only fires when the reply actually depicts release, so arousal stayed pegged at max and the refractory/afterglow cycle never started.
- **Fix:** Kept the sound design premise (arousal is a DESIRE meter, not a climax countdown — a character merely *aching* while untouched must not spontaneously orgasm) but stopped forbidding release outright. The peak-tier note now gates autonomous climax on *active stimulation*: if the scene is physically sexual and stimulation continues, the character is "right at the very edge and should be allowed to tip over into climax naturally, in their own voice, of their own accord — do NOT hold them back waiting for an explicit command"; if nothing physical is happening, the desire≠climax guard still applies ("do NOT orgasm out of nowhere"). This mirrors the structure already used in the 60–80 tier ("could climax with continued stimulation"), which was never broken. No OOC prompt needed anymore, and the refractory/afterglow cycle now engages on its own.
- **Parity:** `nsfw_injection.dart` is the single shared builder for 1:1 and group (charName resolves per active speaker), so the change is parity-safe by construction — both paths get identical wording. Web UI builds prompts through this same Dart path (server-side facade), so it inherits the fix with no separate change.
- **Verification:** New unit test asserts the peak-arousal injection no longer contains the old prohibition ("Do NOT write orgasm", "not past it"), now permits autonomous release ("tip over into climax", "Do NOT hold them back"), and still guards the untouched case ("do NOT orgasm out of nowhere"). `flutter test test/services/chat/prompt_injection_test.dart` — 12/12 pass. `flutter analyze` on the changed file — No issues found.
- **Commit:** (pending user review)

## 2026-07-06 — Release-promotion runbook + guarded script; Rawhide README refresh

- **Files:** scripts/promote-rawhide-to-main.sh (NEW), docs/release-promotion.md (NEW), README.md (refresh).
- **Reason:** Merging Rawhide → main for a stable release has repeatedly mangled release.yml/nightly.yml. Root cause (diagnosed this session): main is the DEFAULT branch, so its workflow copies are live (the nightly cron runs from the default branch), and both branches carry independently hand-edited copies of the big CI YAML — so a 3-way merge forces a human to hand-resolve 50 KB of YAML (the actual corruption). Also found the local clone was shallow (no merge-base → every file an add/add conflict); had to `git fetch --unshallow`. Verified Rawhide is a functional superset of main (chargen split, BYAF importer, TTS emoji-strip, 600s image timeout, full 37-file Character Creator all already on Rawhide), so a "Rawhide wins" promotion loses nothing functional.
- **Script (`scripts/promote-rawhide-to-main.sh`):** builds a `release/promote-<date>-<sha>` candidate whose tree == Rawhide's, EXCEPT a guard list kept from main (`README.md`, `docs/main.md` — override via `GUARD_PATHS`). Mechanism: `git merge -s ours --no-commit Rawhide` → `git read-tree -u --reset Rawhide` → restore guarded paths from main → commit (merge commit, parents [main, Rawhide], so ancestry stays connected for the next cut). Then hard gates: workflows (and release.yml specifically) == Rawhide verbatim; each guard == main; tree differs from Rawhide ONLY in guarded paths; no conflict markers; every workflow YAML parses. ## 2026-07-06 — Fix: completed quests never retired, blocking the next autonomous main quest

- **Files:** lib/services/chat/objective_proposal.dart (`checkTaskCompletionInBackground` + header doc), test/services/chat/objective_proposal_test.dart (1 test updated to the new behavior, +1 new test).
- **Reason:** User report: once every task of an objective is completed, the app never clears the finished task list nor the quest itself. The completion loop had `if (currentTask == null && tasks.isNotEmpty) continue;` — an objective whose tasks were all done was skipped forever, staying `active`+`isPrimary` in the DB. That permanently blocked the next main quest: the realism narrative/one-shot proposal prompt only offers goals "DISTINCT from their current main quest" when a primary exists, and `becomesPrimary = getPrimaryObjective() == null` means an autonomous proposal can only claim the main-quest slot when no primary is active. Net effect: after finishing one quest, a character could never start another.
- **Fix:** Two changes inside the existing check pass (no new methods): (1) an objective found with all tasks complete is now retired via the existing `deactivateObjective` cb + reload (same path the taskless-YES branch already used), fires the journal event kick (`anyCompleted`), and — because the branch runs on every check pass — self-heals quests already stuck from before the fix in existing chats; (2) when the YES path marks the *last* open task complete (pre-mark open count <= 1), the quest retires in the same pass instead of lingering one extra turn. Deactivation (active=false) keeps the row as history; it simply leaves `_activeObjectives`, freeing the `primaryObjective` getter.
- **Parity:** The check operates on `_activeObjectives`, which the group path repoints per speaker (`_loadObjectivesForCurrentSpeaker`); retire uses the same cbs both modes already share, so 1:1 and group behavior stay identical by construction. Web UI reads objectives through the same Dart facade — inherits the fix with no web-side change.
- **Verification:** `flutter analyze` — No issues found. `dart fix --dry-run` — Nothing to fix. `flutter test test/services/chat/` — 488/488 pass (includes the updated "all tasks already completed → quest retired" test and the new "retires only when last open task" test). Header test-count notes synced (15→16).

## 2026-07-09 — Image Studio: LoRA compatibility guard (confidence-driven)

- **Reason:** The Studio's LoRA picker listed every LoRA regardless of the selected checkpoint's base model. Choosing an SD1.5 LoRA on an SDXL checkpoint (or a Flux/SD3/Pony mismatch) produces noise or a hard tensor-shape crash — a footgun with no signal to the user.
- **Investigation finding:** LoRAs came back as bare filename strings from all three local backends. But A1111's `/sdapi/v1/loras` carries a `metadata` block (`ss_base_model_version` / `modelspec.architecture`) we were discarding, and ComfyUI exposes the same via `/view_metadata/loras?filename=`. Draw Things' full gRPC contract (Echo/FilesExist/UploadFile/Pubkey/Hours) has NO per-model version RPC — its listing is the `Echo("models")` filename hack — so DT stays name-heuristic (its filenames are canonical). Web UI has no LoRA control at all; character creator delegates to the Studio. So scope is Studio-desktop only.
- **Design (user-approved, confidence-driven):** detect a base-model family (SD1.5/SDXL/Pony/SD3/Flux/Unknown) from metadata where available (a fact) or the filename (a guess). Hide a LoRA only when metadata *confirms* a hard mismatch (tucked behind a "Show N incompatible" drawer); name-only guesses and Pony↔SDXL soft mismatches are shown + badged "likely", never hidden; unknowns always shown. A warning banner fires whenever the *selected* LoRA mismatches, even one pulled from the drawer.
- **Files:**
  - `lib/services/image/model_family.dart` (NEW, pure) — `ModelFamily` enum, `LoraOption`, `LoraCompat`, `detectFromName` / `detectFromMetadata` / `classifyLora` (metadata wins, name is floor, name-"pony" overrides SDXL metadata) / `compatibility` (name-only mismatch downgraded certain→likely; Pony↔SDXL always likely; unknown either side → unknown).
  - `lib/services/comfy_ui_service.dart` — added `fetchLoraMetadata` (`/view_metadata/loras`, best-effort, empty map on failure).
  - `lib/services/image_gen_service.dart` — the 3 LoRA fetchers now return `List<LoraOption>`: A1111 captures the previously-discarded `metadata`; ComfyUI enriches per-LoRA via metadata in concurrent batches of 8; Draw Things classifies by name.
  - `lib/ui/image_studio/lora_picker.dart` (NEW) — the compatibility-aware picker widget (dropdown of visible + drawer for certain-incompatible + selected-mismatch banner + weight slider), AppColors-only, warm-porch semantics.
  - `lib/ui/image_studio/generation_options_tab.dart` — `_localLoras` now `List<LoraOption>`; replaced the plain dropdown + weight slider block with `LoraPicker`; checkpoint family derived from `st.imageGenModel`; removed the now-dead `_dragLoraWeight` field.
  - Tests: `test/services/image/model_family_test.dart` (NEW, 16 cases — detection, precedence, full compatibility matrix). Updated the fake service in `test/ui/image_studio/generation_options_tab_test.dart` for the new return type.
- **WebUI parity:** maintainer explicitly approved keeping the web image panel simpler (no LoRA selector / advanced features) — the desktop-only advanced tradeoff is accepted, so no web counterpart is required for this work.
- **Draw Things verification:** re-confirmed at the maintainer's request against the generated gRPC stub (`imageService_pb2_grpc.py`) — the DT server serves exactly 6 RPCs (GenerateImage, FilesExist, UploadFile, Echo, Pubkey, Hours); there is no per-model version/metadata RPC. DT's own UI filters from a local on-disk model DB not exposed over gRPC. Canonical-filename detection is the confirmed ceiling for DT.
- **Verification:** `flutter analyze` — No issues found (full project). New tests 16/16; comfy + generation_options widget suites green. `flutter build macos --debug` — Built successfully.

## 2026-07-10 — NSFW/lust: permanent post-cooldown negative deltas fixed + human refractory model
- **Why:** User report: after a character's NSFW refractory cooldown ended, EVERY message scored a negative lust delta forever. Three real bugs found: (1) `realism_state_injection` printed the FEATURE toggle as "cooldown active: true" on every turn forever, so the main model kept playing the character as post-climax; (2) the post-cooldown injection ladder flipped to "physically repulsed / will recoil" at arousal ≤ -2 while climax itself set arousal to -3 — so a character exited the cooldown permanently reading as repelled by their own lover, evals scored the coldness negative, and arousal spiralled down; (3) group-only: the cooldown decrement ran in sendMessage BEFORE the group speaker was picked, so the tick landed on the previous speaker's loaded scalars and was discarded by the next load — group cooldowns never counted down at all.
- **Human model (per user request to make it realistic):** negative arousal now means genuine aversion only, never satedness. Climax sets arousal to 0 (sated-neutral; the cooldown carries "not right now"). During the refractory, eval deltas are halved and floored at -10 (a spent body is hard to stir and impossible to disgust by closeness). On expiry the total resets and lingering negative arousal halves toward neutral. The negative injection ladder is now a spectrum (-60 repulsed / -20 closed-off / <0 simply not in the mood) instead of a cliff at -2, and the eval prompt tells the scorer that refractory low-desire is contented satedness, not rejection.
- **Files (lib):**
  - `lib/services/chat/nsfw_service.dart` — `applyClimaxEffects` arousal -3 → 0; `decrementCooldownIfActive` expiry resets total + halves negative arousal; NEW `applyEvalArousalDelta(int) → int` (the ONE eval apply path, both multi-call and one-shot — returns the delta that actually landed for chips/revert exactness); class doc rewritten to describe the human model instead of the old refactor log.
  - `lib/services/chat/realism_evals.dart` — both arousal apply sites route through `applyEvalArousalDelta`; pending metadata now records the EFFECTIVE delta (regen revert stays exact); both eval prompt call sites pass `refractoryTurnsLeft`.
  - `lib/services/chat/realism_prompt_builder.dart` — `_arousalSection` gained a refractory NOTE (gentle deltas; satedness ≠ rejection); `emotionalEvalPrompt`/`oneShotEvalPrompt` gained `refractoryTurnsLeft` (default 0 — shared section keeps one-shot vs normal parity by construction).
  - `lib/services/chat/prompt_injection/realism_state_injection.dart` — honest state line: refractory shown only while actually running ("post-climax refractory: N of M turns left — sated and recovering, not averse"); nothing printed when the feature is off.
  - `lib/services/chat/prompt_injection/nsfw_injection.dart` — post-cooldown negative-arousal ladder rewritten (repulsed only ≤ -60; closed-off ≤ -20; "not in the mood" < 0; softened neutral).
  - `lib/services/chat_service.dart` — sendMessage cooldown tick gated to 1:1 (`_activeGroup == null`).
  - `lib/services/chat/chat_service_realism_dance.dart` — group per-speaker cooldown tick added right after that speaker's scalars load, saved back to the per-char map immediately (mirrors the per-speaker needs decay; fixes group cooldowns never counting down).
  - `lib/services/chat/needs_simulation.dart` — dead-code audit: deleted the four never-used NSFW callbacks (`getArousalLevel`/`getNsfwCooldownEnabled`/`getCooldownTurnsRemaining`/`setArousalLevel`) — leftovers from the removed suppression buffers; ~119 lines of no-op closure plumbing removed across chat_service + 5 test files.
- **Files (test):** `nsfw_service_test.dart` — climax/expiry tests updated + NEW applyEvalArousalDelta coverage (normal clamp + refractory damp/floor + effective-delta return); dead callback args removed from `needs_simulation_test.dart` (+ helper params), `needs_impact_evaluator_test.dart`, `prompt_injection_test.dart`, `realism_parity_test.dart`, `test/golden/support/fakes.dart`.
- **Parity:** 1:1 vs group — tick is once per response turn in both modes; all mutations live in shared NsfwService methods. One-shot vs normal — same `_arousalSection` fragment and same `applyEvalArousalDelta` apply path by construction. Regen revert exact (metadata stores the landed delta).
- **Verification:** `flutter analyze` — 0 issues from these files (remaining errors are the concurrent Expression Pack UI agent's in-flight files). 118/118 tests pass across nsfw_service, needs_simulation, needs_impact_evaluator, prompt_injection, realism_parity, realism_evals suites.

## 2026-07-10 — Vision QC engine half (image-send path, ExpressionPackQc, describePortrait, active-LLM vision resolver)
- **Why:** Phase 5 of the Image Studio overhaul needs the app's ACTIVE text LLM to actually see images: an advisory Vision QC pass that compares each generated expression-pack image against the base portrait ("same person? expression reads? visual flaws?") and a portrait-describe call that grounds pack prompts in the character's real appearance. This is the engine half; the UI half (grid badges, dialog wiring) ships concurrently in lib/ui/image_studio/.
- **Files (lib):**

## 2026-07-10 — Phase 6: tool-calling verdicts from provider metadata (OpenRouter / Nano-GPT skip the runtime ping)
- **Why:** the tool-calling pill and every tools-first eval pass answered "does this model speak tools?" with a runtime ping (one tiny tool call). OpenRouter and Nano-GPT publish that answer in their /models metadata (`supported_parameters` contains "tools" / `capabilities.tool_calling` — verified live: nano-gpt.com lists 612 models, 208 with tool_calling, 245 with vision), so those two providers can be answered instantly, free, and without touching the model. The parsing existed unconsumed since the vision-capability phase; this consumes it.
- **Design — pre-seed, not per-site branches:** everything already funnels through ONE in-memory `ToolTransportProbe` keyed by `_evalBackendIdentity`. The auto-test path (`ToolSupportTester.onBackendMaybeChanged`) now asks a new optional `fetchMetadataToolVerdict` callback FIRST (`_seedOrTest`): metadata true/false → `markSupported`/`markXmlOnly` on the shared probe (all three eval gates — fireStructuredEval, Journal, Growth — and the pill short-circuit automatically, zero per-site edits); null (local backend, generic host, oMLX, entry miss, fetch failure) → the runtime ping exactly as before. The pill's tap-to-retest still always fires the real ping and can overrule stale metadata (a live tool call is stronger evidence). Identity-switch-mid-fetch guarded like the ping path.
- **Files (lib):**
  - `lib/services/capability/model_capabilities.dart` (143) — shared host helpers `isCapabilityMetadataProviderUrl` / `isNanoGptUrl` (single source for the provider classification).
  - `lib/services/capability/vision_support_resolver.dart` (308) — new `_capsCache` (raw `ModelApiCapabilities` per '$apiUrl::$modelName', misses cached; cleared by `clear()`) + public `capabilitiesForRemote(...)`; `_computeRemote` refactored onto it, so ONE metadata fetch now serves BOTH the vision verdict and the tool verdict.
  - `lib/ui/widgets/vision_projector_field.dart` — `RemoteVisionPill._isMetadataProvider` now delegates to the shared helper (deleted the duplicated host check).
  - `lib/services/chat/tool_support_tester.dart` (176) — optional `fetchMetadataToolVerdict` cb + `_seedOrTest` (metadata first, ping fallback; only stamps when the verdict is still untested and the identity unchanged).
  - `lib/services/chat_service.dart` — wires the cb (gated to `BackendType.openRouter`; oMLX and locals return null → ping path) + resolver import.
- **Files (test):** `tool_support_test.dart` +4 tests (metadata true/false seeds without pinging; null/throwing fetch falls through to ping; mid-fetch model switch records nothing; force retest overrules wrong metadata); `model_capabilities_test.dart` + host-helper group.
- **Verification:** `flutter analyze` — No issues found; 64/64 across tool_support + model_capabilities + realism_evals suites; `flutter build macos --debug` ✓. All touched files <500 lines.
- **Commit:** 71f4025

- **Why:** `BackendType.pseudoRemote` was a redundant second local path — it ran the SAME KoboldCpp subprocess as `kobold`, differing only in that it launched from a `.kcpps` preset via `--config`. But the local `kobold` backend already accepts `kcppsPath` in `startKobold`, already launches presets, and `generateStream` on both used the identical `streamOpenAiChat` transport. Two code paths for one behavior = duplicated UI (radios/chips in three places), a separate service (`PseudoRemoteService`, 413 lines), extra DI, and a standing parity risk. User decision: full merge, remove the mode; presets become a launch option of Local.
- **Fix:** deleted `lib/services/pseudo_remote_service.dart` and `BackendType.pseudoRemote`. `LLMProvider` reduced to kobold/openRouter/omlx (isLocal/hasManagedProcess now key off kobold only); `SetupService` autostart branch merged (one condition handles plain model OR preset-owns-model); DI in `main.dart` dropped the provider (ProxyProvider5→4 for LLMProvider, 4→3 for SetupService) and the window-close/installer-shutdown stop calls. UI: removed the Pseudo-Remote radio (`settings_page.dart`), toggle (`model_settings_dialog.dart` — deleted `_buildPseudoRemoteSettings`/`_startPseudoRemote`/`_stopManagedBackend`, all redundant with `_buildLocalSettings` which already has a KcppsSelector + preset-aware start), chip (`character_creator/steps/setup_step.dart` — the creator's Kobold section already exposes a preset picker in its collapsible extra-settings), and `creator_state`'s `startPseudoRemote`/`stopPseudoRemote`/`isReloadingPseudoRemote` (reloadKoboldWithModel already handles presets). `kobold_log_dialog.dart`/`ai_engine_status_card.dart` collapsed their dual-service reads to KoboldCpp only. WebUI parity: dropped the option from `settings_facade.dart` backend list + enum map (legacy `'pseudoRemote'` string now parses to kobold) and `web_ui/src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx`.
- **Migration (additive, no data loss):** `BackendSettings.load()` rewrites a persisted `backend_type=='pseudoRemote'` to `'kobold'`, carries the old `autostart_pseudo_remote` intent into the single `autostart_backend` flag, and removes the orphaned key. `_syncFromStorage` also treats the legacy string as kobold defensively.
- **Files:** `lib/services/{llm_provider,setup_service,services}.dart`, `lib/services/storage/settings/backend_settings.dart`, `lib/services/storage_service.dart`, `lib/services/web/facade/settings_facade.dart`, `lib/main.dart`, `lib/ui/pages/{settings_page,chat_page}.dart`, `lib/ui/dialogs/{model_settings_dialog,kobold_log_dialog}.dart`, `lib/ui/widgets/ai_engine_status_card.dart`, `lib/ui/character_creator/{creator_state,creator_state_engine}.dart` + `steps/setup_step.dart`, `lib/services/capability/vision_support_resolver.dart` (+ several doc-comment updates), `web_ui/src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx`; test doubles in `test/golden/support/{fakes,fakes_services}.dart` + two golden test files; regenerated the SetupStep/ModelSettings goldens (one fewer backend chip/radio).

## 2026-07-12 (UTC) — Nightly: skip the build when Rawhide hasn't moved
- **File changed:** `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` (Rawhide).
- **Reason:** Daily nightlies were rebuilt+published every 07:00 UTC even when Rawhide had zero new commits since the last one — churning identical artifacts and spurious "Nightly …" releases.
- **How:** Added a `should_build` gate in the `resolve` job. It reads the most recent `nightly-rawhide.<date>.<sha>` release, prefix-matches that trailing short-sha against the current full HEAD sha, and if they're the same commit it emits `should_build=false`; the `nightly` build, `publish-nightly`, and `publish-aur-beta` jobs are `if:`-gated on it. Manual `workflow_dispatch` gains a `force` checkbox to rebuild the same commit anyway. Fails safe: any parse ambiguity or missing prior release builds (never a false skip).
- **NOTE — main:** Scheduled (cron) runs execute the DEFAULT branch's copy of the workflow, so this only affects daily builds once `main`'s `nightly.yml` carries the gate. `main`'s copy is older (no `resolve` job) — pending owner decision on how to sync.

## 2026-07-12 (UTC) — Pre-1.0 stability: the four Tier-1 bugs from the release audit
- **Context:** A 7-way audit (4 Claude agents + 2 Grok reviews, findings cross-verified in code) ahead of the Rawhide→main 1.0 promotion. These are the four release blockers.
- **1. Save chain poisoning + cross-chat overwrite** (`lib/services/chat/chat_service_session_state.dart`): `_saveChat` chained every save onto `_saveChain` with no error handling — one `_doSaveChat` throw (SQLite busy from Character Card Forge's direct writes, or the session id nulled mid-save) turned the chain into an errored future and every later save silently never ran again for the whole app session. Separately, `_doSaveChat` re-read the LIVE `_currentSessionId` after its awaits, so switching chats mid-save could delete the NEW chat's messages and replace them with the OLD chat's snapshot. Fixed by (a) `catchError` on the chain (logs, keeps the chain alive) and (b) capturing `sessionId` + the per-session gen-settings JSON once at `_doSaveChat` entry — everything below uses the captured locals.
- **2. v37 migration boot-loop** (`lib/database/database.dart`): the v36→v37 `ALTER TABLE sessions ADD COLUMN selected_look_avatar_id` was the only unguarded step in the chain. Drift rewrites `user_version` even when an OLDER binary opens a newer DB (rollback, dual-run), so the step can re-run against a DB that already has the column → "duplicate column" → drift caches the error → every query fails → permanent "Database Issue Detected" boot loop on a healthy DB. Wrapped in the same `try/catch` the v34 ALTERs use.
- **3. Group regen/swipe/delete never reverted realism state** (`lib/services/chat/chat_service_reprocess.dart`, `chat_service_speaker_objectives.dart`, `chat_service.dart`): the entire regen revert block was gated `_activeGroup == null`, so group regens stacked the new turn's bond/trust/arousal/needs deltas on top of the rejected turn's (never reverted) ones, plus a second decay tick — permanent per-member drift. Fix: resolve the rejected speaker, load their `_groupRealism` entry into the scalars (the same dance the per-speaker eval uses), run the SAME revert 1:1 runs, persist back to the map; the dance inside `_generateResponse` then replays decay+eval from the clean baseline exactly like the turn being replaced. Group nuances handled: per-speaker baseline comes from the speaker's own last stamped message while the shared clock baseline comes from the most recent stamped message of ANY speaker; the mood-decay counter is NOT restored for groups (groups tick it in sendMessage, which regen doesn't replay, so the rejected turn's tick stands for the replacement). An unresolvable speaker (renamed/removed member) skips the revert rather than corrupting the first member. NEW private method (justified): `_restoreRealismStateForSpeaker` — the group-aware wrapper (load → restore → save) now used by swipe navigation, deleteMessage's time-travel rollback, and the regen accepted-swipe restore; without it the same subtle dance would be copy-pasted at three sites. 1:1 behavior at all these sites is byte-identical to before.
- **4. Backups: torn snapshots + dead app after restore** (`lib/services/backup_service.dart`, `lib/database/database.dart`, `lib/main.dart`): `createBackup` did a raw `File.copy` of the live DB (rollback-journal mode — writes mutate the file in place), so the 30-minute auto-backup could capture a torn, unrestorable copy, discovered only at restore time. Now uses `VACUUM INTO` (SQLite writes a transactionally-consistent snapshot); on failure it deletes any partial file and reports failure rather than falling back to a raw copy. The now-orphaned `AppDatabase.checkpoint()` was deleted (dead code). And `_restoreBackup` in main.dart reopened the DB but never rebound the providers/repositories to the new instance ("database was closed" on every action after restoring from the corruption screen) — it now runs the same `_reinitializeAfterImport` rebind+reload sequence the stable import flow uses.
- **Verification:** `flutter analyze` clean, `dart fix --dry-run` nothing, full test suite + independent Grok review of the diff (results recorded in-conversation).
- **Commit hash:** (pending)

## 2026-07-12 (UTC) — Grok review round on the Tier-1 fixes: 5 hardening changes
- **Process:** Both fix bundles were independently reviewed by Grok 4.5 (hostile, self-contained prompts with diff + surrounding source). It confirmed the core fixes (1:1 paths byte-identical; regen stacking correctly eliminated; migration guard + repair backstop complete; VACUUM INTO the right integrity choice) and flagged real gaps, all verified and fixed:
- **1. Group regen zeroed the mood cadence** (`chat_service_reprocess.dart`): the shared revert body sets `_moodDecayCounter = 0` on `mood_delta` as a 1:1 intermediate (baseline restore + re-tick follow). Groups neither restore nor re-tick it, so the zero stuck. Now gated `!isGroupHostRegen`.
- **2. Wrapper could invent needs** (`chat_service_speaker_objectives.dart`): `_restoreRealismStateForSpeaker`'s load→restore→save round-trip runs `initializeFresh()` for a member with no stored needs; if the stamp carried no needs either, save materialized a brand-new vector into their map entry. Now cleared pre-save when neither source had needs.
- **3. Regen speaker force aligned with revert skip** (`chat_service_reprocess.dart`): `setNextSpeaker` used `firstWhere(..., orElse: first member)` — a renamed/removed member silently forced the WRONG character to speak while the revert (correctly) skipped. Both sites now share one exact-name resolve; unresolvable → no force, no revert.
- **4. Backup prune no longer runs after a failed snapshot** (`backup_service.dart`): the daily-retention window slides, so pruning during a persistent VACUUM-failure streak would slowly delete healthy history while writing nothing. Prune is now gated on a successful create; the manual-backup snackbar no longer claims "no database" for a failed snapshot (`backups_page.dart`).
- **5. Restore overlay is honest about rebind failure** (`main.dart`): `_reinitializeAfterImport` now returns success; `_restoreBackup` keeps the overlay up with "close and reopen to finish" instead of dismissing as success when the rebind (or the restore itself) failed — the data on disk is fine, only the live wiring needs the restart.
- **Accepted residuals (documented, follow-up list):** ~10 dialog-level `Provider.of<AppDatabase>` consumers still hold the pre-rebind instance until restart after a corruption-restore (pre-existing, shared with the import flow; worst case is a failed dialog action, not data loss). Group deleteMessage still doesn't roll back the DELETED speaker's map entry (pre-existing M5; comment now says so instead of overclaiming). Non-last swipe rewinding the shared session clock in groups (pre-existing 1:1 semantics made cross-member-visible) — follow-up.
- **Verification:** `flutter analyze` clean; full test suite rerun after hardening (result in-conversation).
- **Commit hash:** (pending)

## 2026-07-12 (UTC) — Pre-1.0 stability: Tier-2 fixes from the release audit (8)
- **Context:** The second batch from the 7-way pre-promotion audit. All analyze-clean, full suite 2013/2013, Grok review pending.
- **1. Cancel realism eval actually aborts + stops forging a message** (`chat_service_realism_dance.dart`, `chat_service_generation.dart`, `chat_service.dart`): the dance consumed `_realismEvalCancelled` before the caller's abort check could read it, so pressing Cancel let generation proceed anyway; meanwhile `cancelRealismEval` appended a "Realism evaluation interrupted…" line ATTRIBUTED TO THE CHARACTER that permanently rode history/prompts/RAG/journal. Now the dance leaves the flag for its caller (1:1 sendMessage already checked it; group `_generateResponse` now checks it right after the dance and early-returns, hand-clearing the entry-state flags), and the interruption is a transient banner (`_setGuestStatus`), never a chat message.
- **2. One-shot eval no longer freezes the clock (+ uses corrected text)** (`realism_evals.dart`, `time_service.dart`): the deterministic time tick lived only in the multi-call path, so One-Shot mode froze time forever — violating the one-shot parity contract. `evaluateTimeProgressAndPostureIfNeeded` gained `oneShotMode` (ticks the clock + runs the hold/new_day eval when due; skips only the posture-only calls since posture rides the fused JSON) and the one-shot eval now calls it. Also, the one-shot scene-field parses (objective/emotion/intensity/posture/fixation/reason) now read the Director-CORRECTED text, matching the multi-call path (only relationship deltas did before).
- **3. Group needs/bond parity trio** (`needs_simulation.dart`, `chat_service_realism_dance.dart`, `relationship_service.dart`, `chat_service.dart`): (a) new `decayedValueFor` is THE single decay rule (rate + modifier pipeline + clamp) shared by the 1:1 tick, the group tick, and the group per-speaker decay — group members now get the conditional decay modifiers (low energy → faster hunger, etc.) that were 1:1-only; (b) short-term bond decay moved from `sendMessage` (pre-speaker-pick, hit the first member under random turn order) into the dance after the speaker is pinned; 1:1 keeps its tick; (c) long-term/decay cadence counters now ride each speaker's `_groupRealism` entry via optional `getGroupCounter`/`setGroupCounter` (tests fall back to the legacy shared registers) so growth/decay run on each member's OWN turn count instead of rotation luck.
- **4. Journal/Growth tools transport hardening** (`journal_maintenance.dart`, `growth_service.dart`, `journal_ops.dart`, `growth_ops.dart`, `pass_support.dart`, `llm_service.dart`): an honest-empty tools reply (calls present, zero valid ops) no longer brands the shared backend probe XML-only and re-fires the whole pass (mirrors growth's handling); tool-arg reads use a tolerant `strArg` (was `as String?`, which threw on a non-string and aborted the whole multi-owner pass); transient errors (timeout/5xx/overload via new `looksLikeTransientBackendError`) no longer count as a "no tool support" verdict; and `eventKickPending` is consumed inside the pass (once it starts) so a pass blocked by a parked review or an in-flight pass can't silently eat the kick.
- **5. ComfyUI expression packs no longer fail without an edit workflow** (`comfy_edit_presets.dart`, `expression_pack_dialog.dart`): ComfyUI advertises edit unconditionally (workflow-gated, not model-gated), so packs routed every slot to the edit path and failed on unfilled model slots. New pure `comfyEditReady` gates the pack's edit routing on the same readiness the Edit tab enforces; not ready → img2img fallback.
- **6. Character rename carries its avatar gallery** (`character_repository.dart`): avatar/look folders are keyed on the character's name, so a rename blanked the gallery, stopped expressions resolving, and made `removeAvatar` hit the wrong folder. `updateCharacter` now moves `Characters/<oldSafeName>/` → `<newSafeName>/` (rename when free, else merge files, never overwriting), best-effort so it can't block the rename.
- **7. Web reconnect no longer leaves a stale/ghosted UI** (`ChatPage.tsx`, `useLibrary.ts`, `useStory.ts`): the server's `connected` event had no handler, so a phone waking from sleep never refetched and stayed frozen forever. All three consumers now refetch on reconnect; the chat page also clears the streaming buffer so a missed `done` can't leave a ghost partial bubble that garbles the next reply. Web bundle rebuilt.
- **8. Legacy JSON migration can't wedge the app** (`database.dart`, `main.dart`): `getCharacterByImagePath` used `getSingleOrNull` (throws on a duplicate image_path), which aborted the migration, pinned the app on the migration overlay forever, and re-imported all characters on every retry. It's now a `limit(1)` first-row read (so the migration runs to completion and marks itself done — ending the retry/duplicate cycle), and `_runMigrationIfNeeded` is wrapped so any other throw drops the overlay and opens the app.
- **Verification:** `flutter analyze` clean, `dart fix --dry-run` clean, `tsc --noEmit` clean, full suite 2013/2013.
- **Commit hash:** (pending)

## 2026-07-12 (UTC) — Grok review round on Tier-2: hardening + one honest deferral
- **Process:** Both Tier-2 bundles hostile-reviewed by Grok 4.5 (self-contained diffs). It confirmed the cores (one-shot clock, decay-modifier unification, bond-cadence math, honest-empty, kick ownership) and flagged real issues; each was verified against the code and resolved:
- **Rename media move was a FILE-LOSS ship-blocker** (`character_repository.dart`): the safe-name-collision merge path ran `delete(recursive: true)` on the source AFTER skipping files whose destination already existed — destroying those skipped files. Rewritten to be non-destructive by construction: a colliding file is LEFT at the source (stranded, recoverable, logged), never overwritten or deleted; the source tree is pruned only by removing files just moved, then empty dirs — never a blanket recursive delete. Also reordered to DB-commit-THEN-move so a failed move leaves the (pre-existing) blank-gallery bug, not the worse "DB says new name, files under old" split-brain. Cross-device rename falls back to per-file move.
- **Migration duplicate pick was non-deterministic** (`database.dart`, `data_migration_service.dart`): `getCharacterByImagePath` now orders by `createdAt, id` before `limit(1)` so a duplicate image_path links sessions to the SAME (oldest) twin every run, not a plan-dependent random one. `_migrateCharacters` also gained an idempotent guard (skip a card already imported by imagePath basename) so an aborted-then-retried migration can't multiply duplicates.
- **Cancel flag could bleed to the next turn** (`chat_service.dart`): added a start-of-turn `_realismEvalCancelled = false` clear in `sendMessage` (belt-and-suspenders over the existing `_isEvaluatingRealism` guard). Also fixed a SECOND fake-message path the review surfaced — `onHandleRealismEvalCancelledDuringOnnx` appended a persisted "Interruption" chat line (history/prompt/RAG/journal pollution); now a transient banner like the main cancel path.
- **Transient tools-branding: honest deferral** (`llm_service.dart`, `pass_support.dart`): the `looksLikeTransientBackendError` code added earlier was INERT — `generateWithTools` collapses all failures (incl. 5xx/timeout) to null instead of throwing, so the catch never fires and a transient hiccup on the first probe still brands the backend XML-only for the session. Rather than ship dead code or take a transport-layer change into the freeze, the inert helper was removed and the limitation documented in `pass_support.dart` as a post-1.0 follow-up (needs `generateWithTools` to surface transient errors).
- **Verified-clean (no change needed):** journal honest-empty correctly advances the cursor (non-null empty result settles the window); group needs decay has a single path (only 2 `tickDecay` callers, both 1:1-gated — the dance is the sole group decay); mood-decay speaker id matches the needs-decay speaker (both resolve to the pinned turn speaker); the new group cadence counters persist (the `_groupRealism` map is serialized/parsed wholesale, no key whitelist). Accepted caveat: clearing the web streaming buffer on reconnect can briefly blank a reply if the socket blips mid-generation on that same client — self-heals on the next token; the ghost-bubble fix is worth it.
- **Verification:** `flutter analyze` clean, `dart fix --dry-run` clean, full suite rerun.
